title: English rendering of PM’s address at the Centenary Celebrations of UPSC
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 OCT 2026 1:51PM by PIB Delhi
content:
My colleagues in the Union Cabinet, Dr. Jitendra Singh Ji, P. K. Mishra Ji, T. V. Somanathan Ji, Ajay Kumar Ji, all the esteemed members of the UPSC, Chairpersons of the various State Public Service Commissions who have come from different states, other distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen.
Before I begin today's discussion, I would like to mention an incident that occurred yesterday. The manner in which India's Captain Smita displayed patience, prudence, and courage, and as the Prime Minister of Israel said today, this Indian prevented another 9/11 from taking place. This act of valor by Smita fills every citizen of the country with pride. Today, I also spoke with his father Bhupendra Bhai, his mother Geeta Ben, and his wife Sonal. His treatment is ongoing, and today the entire world is proud of him. I appeal to the people of the country that we should all pray for Smita's long life and excellent health, and salute our brother Smita, who has enhanced India's glory.
Friends,
Today is not only a celebration of 100 years of the UPSC, but also a celebration of a legacy. It is a celebration of the aspirations that millions upon millions of young people cherish and pursue every year. It is a celebration of the trust that every Indian places in this institution. During this century-long journey, generations changed, governments changed, technology changed, and syllabi changed, yet the trust in the UPSC remains just as unwavering today, and that is one of your greatest assets. A commemorative postage stamp and coin marking this 100-year journey have just been released. A compilation of 100 important case laws has also been published. I pay my respects to all the distinguished individuals associated with this century-long journey. I extend my heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to all of you. A little while ago, I was visiting the gallery that has been set up here, and I would encourage all of you to spend 10 to 15 minutes exploring it. I noticed a photograph from the 75th anniversary celebrations in which Lt. General Surendra Nath can be seen. Today, at the age of 90, he is present among us.
Friends,
There are many individuals who transformed this journey into a legacy of trust, introduced changes in tune with the times, and took the institution to new heights. Every one of them deserves appreciation and recognition. While looking through the gallery, I noticed that it also contains information about how Subhas Chandra Bose went through this very process in 1920. What caught my attention was that although India was under British rule at the time, there used to be a Sanskrit paper in the examination, and Subhas Babu wrote his paper in Sanskrit.
Friends,
On this historic occasion, I would also like to pay tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. After Independence, the challenge before him was not merely to keep the nation free. The challenge before him was also to govern and build a nation. The steel frame that was required for the reconstruction of the nation was provided by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. He made this institution one of the principal pillars of independent India and strengthened it.
Friends,
When the foundation of this institution was laid in 1926, the priorities of that era were different. At that time, both the focus of the system and its commitment were directed towards the British Raj. After India attained Independence, the dreams of a free India and the governance needs of a free India became the central focus. Over the past decades, the UPSC has discharged its responsibilities in an exemplary manner. Much has already been said from this stage about its achievements and contributions. Therefore, I neither wish to repeat those points nor go into detail about them. Moving beyond history, we now have India's future waiting before us. One quarter of the 21st century, twenty-five years, has already passed. The next twenty to twenty-five years will be extremely important for India, for every citizen of India, and for every institution of India. Therefore, I would like to focus my discussion today in that direction.
Friends,
For a Developed India, the kind of governance the country now requires depends significantly on the UPSC and the State Public Service Commissions. The young people whom you are recruiting today will play a crucial role in building a Developed India, and they themselves will be among the greatest beneficiaries of a Developed India. Keeping this in mind, we must always remember two touchstones. The first touchstone is: Nation First. The second touchstone is: Citizen First. These are the two standards against which every selection must be measured. When candidates are evaluated in this spirit, and when individuals imbued with this spirit are selected, the achievement of national goals becomes far more natural and far easier.
Friends,
India in 2047 will be very different from the India of today. India will be far more urbanized than it is today. The gap between villages and cities will narrow. The aspirations and expectations of our citizens, especially our youth, will be significantly greater. The signs of this transformation are already visible. Therefore, the question today is not merely one of service delivery. The question is also whether public services are able to keep pace with the speed of today's world of instant delivery. Are they able to move at that pace? Today, citizens do not want to wait weeks or months for a service. When AI can process thousands of documents within moments, and when governments have access to real-time data, citizens expect quick solutions. This changing mindset also demands new changes from our civil services. Therefore, we must align our selection parameters and recruitment processes with the needs of the future. We need to bring into public service those young people who are attracted not by public office, but by public service. Therefore, it is important that recruitment examinations should not merely assess how much a candidate knows. They should also assess why that young person wants to join the civil services. Because when the motivation is right, it becomes easier both to keep pace with changing public aspirations and to adapt to them.
Friends,
Many of you are familiar with the fact that whenever I meet trainee officers, I ask them to write down, right at the beginning and in their own handwriting, why they have joined the civil service. This is because responsibilities increase over time and new challenges emerge. At such moments, that small note reminds them of their original purpose. It also becomes a self-appraisal tool for them. UPSC and the State Commissions may also consider developing a similar mechanism.
Friends,
We have seen that period in the past when it was believed that the government was the ultimate guardian and provider. But today, our mantra is, "Nagrik Devo Bhava" (The Citizen is Divine). In other words, the citizen of this country is no less than a deity for us. Service to the citizen is our highest priority.
Therefore, friends,
Twenty-first-century India is moving forward with a new work culture. Its core principle is: Pro-People, Pro-Active, Good Governance! Pro-People means working not according to the convenience of the government, but by placing the interests of citizens above everything else. Pro-Active means preparing solutions by anticipating problems before they arise, instead of acting only after problems appear. Good Governance means there should be neither absence of government, nor pressure from government, nor unnecessary influence. At both the national and state levels, we must design our selection processes in accordance with this spirit. We must provide the nation with professionals who possess the sensitivity to understand the suffering of the poor; who willingly step forward with youthful energy; who find innovative solutions to difficult challenges; who understand the needs of the nation; who ensure compliance with the law; and who can also judge whether a law is making people's lives easier or whether it is becoming an obstacle.
Friends,
We are all witnessing the rapid pace at which the times are changing and technology is evolving. The period that lies ahead is going to present society with new kinds of challenges. We are all familiar with the global debate currently taking place around AI. In such a scenario, our civil servants too will be required to work under very different circumstances. There will be situations involving information warfare, the challenge of deepfakes, concerns regarding algorithmic bias, and complex questions such as climate justice. Therefore, in our selection processes, we must also give priority to assessing complex problem-solving abilities and long-term vision, and to making deliberate efforts in that direction.
Friends,
We all know that today our nation is moving rapidly on the expressway of reforms. At such a time, our examination-conducting agencies must move quickly on reforms that are the need of the hour. One such important issue is the time taken to conduct examinations. We must not view an examination merely as an event. It is connected not only to an event but to the future and lives of young people. A delay of even a few months in examinations can become a serious challenge for them. Coaching fees, rent, transportation expenses, all of these impose a heavy burden on families. Therefore, it is extremely important that our examination system adopts the principle of time certainty. UPSC and all selection commissions across the country must ensure that, without lowering standards, we find ways to shorten our examination cycle. In fact, while I was looking at the gallery, I noticed that nearly one hundred days have already been reduced. This achievement certainly deserves appreciation, and I congratulate all of you for it.
But friends,
This is not merely an administrative reform. It is also a reform that promotes equity.
Friends,
All of you are aware of the Chief Secretaries' Conference and the DGP Conference. Over the last ten years, these have evolved into important institutional mechanisms. Under these forums, all the Chief Secretaries of the country come together for three days to deliberate and exchange ideas. Similarly, during the DGP Conference, all the Directors General of Police gather for three days to discuss issues and share experiences. One objective of these conferences is to help one state learn about, understand, and, where appropriate, adopt the best practices of another state. I have been informed that every year UPSC organizes a National Conference in partnership with State Public Service Commissions. To make this conference broader, more productive, and richer in new ideas, I am sure you are continuously thinking about giving it a new shape and a new dimension. Such efforts help institutions share their best practices with one another. At the same time, this conference should also study international best practices. Focused discussions should also be held on how technology can be used to improve the efficiency of our processes and procedures. Such efforts at cross-learning will benefit UPSC as well as every state selection commission. We must also consider standardizing procedural norms and processes. This will provide significant assistance to young people.
Friends,
Another important subject is capacity building within UPSC and the state selection commissions. This effort should continue on a sustained basis. The iGOT platform developed under Mission Karmayogi can also be used for our internal systems, for strengthening the capabilities of our teams, and for enhancing the efficiency of our institutions through these various platforms.
Friends,
You must always remember that your work is linked directly to the future of India's youth. In other words, you are an important pillar in the mission of transforming youth power into national power. Over the years, you have played a major role in advancing this mission. When UPSC was established, opportunities were more readily available to young people from large cities, economically privileged families, and prestigious institutions. Today, however, youth from villages and small towns are also entering public service. The participation of our daughters is also steadily increasing. In 1952, women constituted only 3 percent of candidates in the civil services, just three percent. Today that figure has risen to more than 30 percent. In the entire history of UPSC, there have been four women Chairpersons. The time for applause comes now. Out of those four women Chairpersons in UPSC's entire history, three have been appointed after 2014. These changes are not merely statistics; they demonstrate how greatly the scope of opportunity has expanded in our country.
Friends,
In 1976, when UPSC completed fifty years, the number of candidates appearing for examinations was far lower than it is today. Compared to that period, the number of examination aspirants has increased by more than forty-five times. In other words, today we have before us an enormous pool of talent. This is a matter of immense pride for the nation. At the same time, our responsibility has grown proportionately. When we possess such a vast talent pool, one that is the envy of the world, you are not merely selecting a candidate. You are choosing an individual who will later become a representative of the government. At the grassroots level, people will regard that individual as the government itself. Therefore, all of you bear a tremendous responsibility to select the right person.
Friends,
During its first century, UPSC has continuously strengthened its credibility and earned the trust of the nation. Now, as this institution enters its second century, it must enrich and deepen that credibility in accordance with new possibilities and new challenges. While preserving the values that have been our strength until now, we must also upgrade ourselves to meet the demands of the future. UPSC's independence, impartiality, commitment to merit, confidentiality, and fair procedures constitute its defining identity. These values must always be preserved. With this appeal, I once again extend my heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to all of you.
Thank you very much.

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi participated in the Centenary Celebrations of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) today  at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Highlighting the profound legacy behind the centenary in his address, the Prime Minister noted that the 100-year celebration is truly a festival of the immense aspirations lived by millions of youths and the unshakable trust every Indian places in the institution. He praised the organization's enduring credibility despite changing generations, governments, technologies, and syllabi, celebrating the release of a commemorative postage stamp, a special coin, and a compilation of 100 significant case laws.
Recalling the monumental challenges faced after independence, the Prime Minister paid deep homage to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel for establishing the vital steel frame required not just to keep the country independent, but to actively govern the newly formed nation. He praised Sardar Patel for transforming and empowering the institution into a premier pillar of independent India. “The steel frame that was needed for the reconstruction of the nation was provided by Sardar Patel,” noted Shri Modi.
Contrasting the institution's British Raj origins in 1926 with its post-independence evolution, the Prime Minister noted that the system successfully shifted its focus to fulfill the dreams of a free nation. He acknowledged that while the UPSC has excellently discharged its historical duties, the focus must now decisively pivot toward the critical next 25 years that await the country. “Therefore, today I will keep the focus of my discussion in this direction,” asserted Shri Modi.
Detailing the critical role of selection commissions in achieving a Viksit Bharat, the Prime Minister emphasized that the youths recruited today will simultaneously serve as the chief architects and the primary beneficiaries of the nation's future. He mandated that every selection process must be rigorously tested against the dual criteria of prioritizing the nation and the citizen. “When candidates filled with this spirit are selected, achieving national goals will become that much more natural and easier,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Projecting the vastly different socio-economic landscape of 2047, the Prime Minister explained that an increasingly urbanized nation with narrowing rural-urban divides will dramatically elevate the expectations of the youth. He warned that traditional service delivery models must evolve to match the speed of an instant-delivery world where citizens demand rapid, real-time solutions powered by AI. “This changing mindset demands new changes from our Civil Services as well,” observed Shri Modi.
Urging a fundamental shift in recruitment philosophy, the Prime Minister stressed that the selection parameters must evaluate not just academic knowledge, but the underlying motivation to ensure candidates are drawn to public service rather than mere public office. He explained that selecting individuals with the right inherent motivation makes it significantly easier for the administration to adapt to rapidly changing public aspirations. “Therefore, we will also have to adapt our Selection Parameters and Recruitment Process according to future needs,” asserted Shri Modi.
Sharing his personal interactions with newly inducted civil servants, the Prime Minister suggested that trainee officers should write down their original motivations to serve as a grounding self-appraisal tool when future challenges and responsibilities mount. He encouraged both the UPSC and state commissions to institutionalize similar introspective mechanisms for candidates. “UPSC and state commissions can also consider developing such a system,” remarked Shri Modi.
Discarding the archaic 'Mai-Baap' governance mindset of the past, the Prime Minister heralded a modern administrative era built on the absolute principle of 'Nagrik Devo Bhava'- treating the citizen as divine. He declared that placing the service of the citizen above all else is the absolute core of 21st-century governance. “Meaning, the citizen of the country is no less than a deity to us,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Defining the new work culture for modern administration, the Prime Minister explicitly detailed that 21st-century India is moving forward with an entirely fresh operational ethos. He stated that the fundamental principles of this new era rest entirely on three core pillars. “Its fundamental principles are Pro-People, Pro-Active, Good Governance!” asserted Shri Modi.
Elaborating on these foundational governance principles, the Prime Minister demanded that selection processes at both national and state levels be meticulously designed to recruit professionals who proactively anticipate problems and operate without unnecessary pressure or influence. He emphasized the need for empathetic civil servants who find innovative solutions, proactively ease citizens' lives, and critically evaluate the impact of laws on the public. “We have to give the country those professionals who find innovative ways out of difficult problems,” noted Shri Modi.
Addressing the unprecedented technological disruptions facing society, the Prime Minister cautioned that future civil servants will have to navigate entirely new battlegrounds such as information warfare, deepfakes, algorithmic bias, and climate justice. He instructed recruitment agencies to adapt to these global shifts by prioritizing candidates' foresight and complex problem-solving abilities. “In such a scenario, in the selection process, we will also have to give priority to testing complex problem-solving and foresight,” asserted Shri Modi.
Highlighting the urgency of administrative overhauls, the Prime Minister insisted that examination agencies must rapidly align with the nation's broader reform momentum by adopting the principle of Time Certainty to shorten exam cycles without lowering standards. He emphasized that prolonged examinations inflict severe financial burdens, such as coaching fees, rent, and transport, on families, transforming cycle reduction into a fundamental fairness issue. “This will also be an equity reform,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Encouraging systematic institutional capacity building, the Prime Minister praised existing national conferences where state commissions share best practices, but urged them to elevate these forums by studying international standards and focusing on technological efficiency. He advocated for cross-learning and standardizing procedures to provide immense relief and clarity to participating youths across the country. “This process of cross-learning will benefit UPSC as well and will also benefit the selection commissions of every state,” noted Shri Modi.
Reiterating the absolute necessity of continuous institutional growth, the Prime Minister advised that both the UPSC and state selection commissions must relentlessly focus on their own capacity building. He recommended heavily leveraging the digital infrastructure already established under the national mission for civil servants. “The i-GOT platform created under Mission Karmayogi can be utilized for this,” remarked Shri Modi.
Reminding the officials of their profound national duty, the Prime Minister emphasized that their core mission is directly linked to transforming youth power into robust national power, celebrating how opportunities have successfully shifted from elite city-dwellers to talented youth from rural villages. He proudly noted the dramatic rise in female candidates in civil services, jumping from a mere 3 percent in 1952 to over 30 percent today, alongside the historic appointment of three out of four women UPSC Chairpersons post-2014. “These changes are not just statistics; they show how much the scope of opportunities in the country has expanded,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Pointing to the massive explosion in candidate participation since the institution's 50th anniversary in 1976, the Prime Minister noted a 45-fold increase in exam takers, representing a vast national talent pool that demands monumental responsibility from selectors. He reminded the commissions that they are not merely picking candidates, but choosing individuals who will become the very face and representative of the government at the grassroots level. “Therefore, all of you have a very huge responsibility of selecting the right person,” asserted Shri Modi.
Looking toward the institution's second century, the Prime Minister urged the commission to aggressively upgrade its operations to meet future challenges while fiercely protecting its foundational credibility. He stated that the core identity of the UPSC, its independence, impartiality, merit, confidentiality, and fair processes, must remain eternally uncompromised. “These values must always remain,” affirmed Shri Modi.

title: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan calls for making cleanliness a part of everyday public behaviour, not limiting it to campaigns
subtitle: Union Agriculture Minister directs officials to ensure public participation, behavioural change and measurable outcomes in cleanliness activities
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 OCT 2026 6:48PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today emphasised that cleanliness should not remain confined to the duration of a campaign, but should become an integral part of people’s behaviour and everyday lives. Addressing a virtual meeting with the Secretaries and senior officials of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and the Ministry of Rural Development, he called for active participation by officials and employees in cleanliness activities and urged them to lead by example. He also stressed the need to continuously strengthen awareness and participation around cleanliness in offices, workplaces, field offices and rural areas. Shri Chouhan said that sustained efforts, rather than activities limited to a defined campaign period, are essential to make cleanliness a lasting practice and a shared responsibility across institutions and communities.
Shri Chouhan said that
Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
requires extensive public participation to ensure that cleanliness activities are both effective and sustainable. He directed officers and employees to give priority to cleanliness within their respective areas of work and to take the initiative themselves rather than treating such activities merely as an official requirement. He placed particular emphasis on effectively connecting rural areas, panchayats and field-level offices with cleanliness activities and ensuring the participation of farmers, rural communities, sanitation workers, the media and other relevant stakeholders. He stressed that the involvement of these groups is important for taking cleanliness efforts beyond government offices and making them more visible and meaningful at the grassroots level. Active participation by all concerned, he said, would help create greater awareness and encourage cleanliness to become part of routine practices in communities.
The Union Minister directed that cleanliness activities should not be reduced to a formality, but should produce clear and measurable outcomes. He emphasised the need for systematic documentation of the work undertaken as part of the campaign so that the results and impact of the activities can be properly assessed. Wherever possible, he called for achievements to be recorded through before-and-after photographs, enabling the changes brought about through cleanliness initiatives to be clearly documented. He stressed that such documentation would help demonstrate the tangible results of the campaign and ensure that the work undertaken is properly recorded for future review. The focus, he said, should remain on visible improvements, measurable outcomes and sustained efforts rather than simply completing activities within the stipulated campaign period.
During the meeting, Shri Atish Chandra, Secretary, Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare; Dr Mangi Lal Jat, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General, Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR); Shri Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Department of Rural Development; and Shri P Narhari, Joint Secretary, Department of Land Resources, briefed the Union Minister on cleanliness activities being undertaken by their respective departments and shared details of their forthcoming action plans. The officials outlined the work already undertaken as well as the proposed activities and priorities for the next phase. Their presentations covered the participation of officials and employees, activities at field and institutional levels, and measures being planned to further strengthen cleanliness efforts across the departments and their associated offices and institutions.
The meeting was informed about various activities undertaken by the Department of Agriculture under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 from September 16 to October 2. These included cleanliness pledges, Swachh Pathshala activities, participation of young people, solid waste management, cleanliness drives across office premises, and intensive cleaning of corridors, canteens and toilets at headquarters and field offices. Activities also included the disposal of old furniture and electronic waste as part of efforts to improve cleanliness and make more effective use of available office space. The meeting was also informed about initiatives undertaken to honour sanitation workers, conduct health check-ups for them and organise various activities for their children. These efforts were aimed at recognising the contribution of sanitation workers while also supporting their welfare and encouraging wider participation in cleanliness-related activities. The meeting also reviewed efforts to involve employees directly in cleanliness work and to strengthen awareness around responsible waste management.
It was informed during the meeting that the disposal and auction of old furniture and electronic waste had generated
revenue of approximately Rs 15 lakh
. In addition, officials and employees participated in collective cleanliness drives through
shramdaan
(volunteering), contributing their time and effort to activities undertaken as part of the campaign. A plan was also shared to take forward activities under the
‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’
campaign. The initiatives discussed during the meeting reflected efforts to combine cleanliness activities with responsible disposal of unused material, greater participation by officials and employees, and activities aimed at creating a cleaner and more organised working environment. The revenue generated through the disposal and auction of old furniture and electronic waste also highlighted the value of identifying and appropriately disposing of material that is no longer required.
Regarding the
Special Campaign to be conducted from October 2 to October 31, 2026
, all departments shared details of the targets set for the disposal of pending files and cases, reduction in the number of pending matters, disposal of scrap and e-waste, better utilisation of office space and removal of unusable material. As part of the campaign, unused computers, printers and other electronic equipment will be identified and processed for disposal in accordance with the prescribed rules and procedures. The progress made against the identified targets will be reviewed regularly, while achievements will be appropriately documented. The exercise will focus not only on physical cleanliness but also on improving the efficiency and organisation of offices by addressing pending matters, removing redundant material and ensuring better use of available space. Regular monitoring and documentation will help departments assess progress against their respective targets and record the outcomes of the campaign in a systematic manner.
The Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE), and the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) informed the meeting that a large-scale cleanliness campaign was being conducted at the Pusa campus, with officers, employees and students actively participating in the activities. Similar cleanliness-related activities are also being conducted across all ICAR institutes and Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs). Through the KVK network, efforts are being made to connect farmers and rural communities with cleanliness, waste management and environmental awareness. These activities are intended to extend the message of cleanliness beyond institutional premises and strengthen awareness among farming and rural communities. The participation of students, employees, officers, farmers and rural communities is also helping to create wider engagement with cleanliness and responsible waste management at different levels. The meeting was informed that the network of ICAR institutions and KVKs is being used to support these efforts and encourage greater awareness of cleanliness and environmental responsibility among people in rural areas.
Shri Chouhan called upon all concerned officers and employees not to limit cleanliness to the prescribed duration of the campaign, but to make it a continuous part of everyday behaviour in offices, villages, panchayats and workplaces. He said the success of a cleanliness campaign should not be measured only by the physical cleaning of premises. Its real impact must be reflected through behavioural change, public participation and sustainable outcomes that continue beyond the campaign period. He emphasised that cleanliness should become a regular practice and a shared responsibility rather than an activity undertaken only during designated campaigns. By encouraging participation, maintaining awareness and ensuring measurable and lasting results, cleanliness efforts can have a sustained impact across workplaces, rural areas and communities. The Union Minister stressed that the objective should ultimately be to make cleanliness an enduring part of daily life and public behaviour.

title: ICAR and FCI signs MoU for Safe and Sustainable Foodgrain Storage
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 OCT 2026 5:47PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the Food Corporation of India (FCI) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on 30 September 2026 to undertake research on alternative fumigation technologies for safe and sustainable management of storage pests in wheat and rice. The research study is supported by the Department of Food & Public Distribution (DFPD), Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution.
The two-year Phase-I project will be implemented by ICAR–Central Institute of Post-Harvest Engineering and Technology (CIPHET), Ludhiana.
For decades, India's critical grain reserves have relied heavily on aluminium phosphide (ALP) and malathion for post-harvest pest control. However, widespread and repeated use has led to severe consequences, including
pest resistance
frequencies reaching 72-100% in key Indian states and escalating fumigation cycles that drive up operational costs. Furthermore, current chemical methods pose significant respiratory threats to workers and long-term ecological risks. This initiative seeks to directly address these challenges by standardizing the commercial use of nitrogen gas, carbon dioxide (
C
O
2
), and a synergistic combination of
C
O
2
and phosphine. The following three major trials will be conducted in Phase-I:
Nitrogen gas (>99%) fumigation for effective management of storage pests in wheat stored in metal silos.
Combined carbon dioxide and phosphine gas fumigation for managing/controlling storage pests in wheat and rice stored in bags at FCI/CWC warehouses.
Carbon dioxide fumigation for managing/controlling storage pests in wheat and rice in bags enclosed in hermetic covers.
Following the two-year Phase-I pilot, Phase-II will expand into a one-year multi-location trial across varied agro-climatic zones to establish region-specific Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
The initiative aims to develop scientifically validated, scalable and sustainable alternatives to conventional chemical fumigation, addressing concerns related to increasing pest resistance, occupational exposure, environmental impacts and fumigant residues.
The MoU was signed in the presence of the Dr. M. L Jat, Secretary, DARE & Director General, ICAR; Dr. Rajbir Singh, Deputy Director General (Agricultural Engineering), Dr. D.K. Yadav Deputy Director General (Crop Science), Dr. K. Narsaiah, Assistant Director General (Processing Engineering); ICAR. The MoU was signed by Dr. Nachiket Kotwaliwale, Director, ICAR-CIPHET and Dr. A.K. Sinha, Executive Director (Quality Control), FCI. The event was also attended by Ms. Priya Jacob, Director, DFPD, Sh. Rajagopal General Manager QC-FCI, Dr. Devinder Dhingra, Pr. Scientist, ICAR; Dr. Sandeep Mann Pr. Scientist and Lead Investigator of project, ICAR-CIPHET; Shri Gautam Kumar, Deputy General Manager (Quality Control), FCI; Sh CP Saharan and Ms. Sarika Pritam, Assistant General Manager (Quality Control), FCI.

title: Department of Agricultural Research and Education - Indian Council of Agricultural Research’s  Swachhata Hi Seva 2026: From Participation to a Viksit Bharat
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 OCT 2026 3:09PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), along with its 114 Institutes, Regional Centres, Agricultural Technology Application Research Institutes (ATARIs) and Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), is participating in the fortnight-long Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 campaign from 17 September to 2 October 2026 under the theme “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat”. The campaign is being implemented across the ICAR system in both letter and spirit, in accordance with the prescribed five-pillar framework and the date-wise action plan. It commenced on 17th September 2026 with the Swachhata Pledge administered by the Secretary, DARE & DG, ICAR, in the presence of senior officers, including the AS&FA, and was also introduced through video conferencing to ICAR Institutes and establishments across the country.
For wider dissemination and outreach, Press releases have been issued by ICAR Headquarters on the activities undertaken under the campaign, while ICAR Institutes and establishments have also been independently undertaking publicity and outreach through local print media, display of banners and other appropriate communication channels. At both Headquarters and institutional levels, the campaign and its activities are also being disseminated through social media platforms, including Facebook, X and Instagram, thereby extending the message of Swachhata beyond the ICAR network to wider and more diverse audiences, particularly digitally engaged audiences and the younger generation, including Gen Z.
Major Activities under the Five Pillars
1.Transformation of Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs) and Clean Public Places
Under this pillar, ICAR Institutes and establishments have undertaken identification and transformation of black and dark spots across urban and rural areas, including locations such as bus stands along highways, institutional premises, research fields and other public spaces. Cleanliness drives have been complemented by beautification and improvement of these spaces, with participation of staff, students and local communities, wherever applicable, to create visibly cleaner and more welcoming public areas.
2. Swachh Paathshala: Yuva for Swachhata
Under this pillar, ICAR Institutes, ATARIs and KVKs have actively engaged students and youth in Swachhata activities, harnessing their zeal and enthusiasm through cleanliness drives, awareness activities, demonstrations, competitions and other participatory initiatives. The emphasis has been on inculcating the values of Swachhata among young participants so that these values are imbibed as part of their everyday conduct and sustained beyond the campaign.
3. Safai Mitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir
Under this pillar, ICAR Institutes and establishments have undertaken activities focused on the safety, health, dignity and social welfare of Safai Mitras. Efforts have included promoting awareness and access to social welfare schemes, including VB-GRAMG and PMAY, along with cleanliness of public toilets and other sanitation facilities. The activities also seek to reinforce Mahatma Gandhi’s message that no work is menial or insignificant, while recognising the dignity and contribution of those engaged in sanitation and cleanliness.
4. Jan Bhagidari
for Swachhata
Under this pillar, ICAR Institutes and establishments have promoted active participation in Swachhata activities, with a focus on environmental responsibility and the role of citizens as major stakeholders in maintaining clean public spaces. This has included cleanliness drives at Visarjan sites, riverbanks, ghats and other public areas, along with Clean Green Festivities, eco-friendly and zero-waste celebrations, composting of flower waste and offerings, and other community-oriented initiatives.
The campaign has also included a focus on Swachh Tourist Spots, with emphasis on promoting Swachhata at ASI monuments, tourist destinations and other public spaces, including through cleanliness drives and illumination of monuments with the Swachhata message. These efforts seek to draw greater public attention to the cleanliness and upkeep of heritage and tourist spaces, while encouraging responsible tourism and greater citizen participation in maintaining such places.
5. Swachhata Se Samriddhi
Under this pillar, ICAR Institutes and establishments have promoted the principles of Reduce, Reuse and Recycle through activities such as Waste to Art, Kabaad Se Jugaad, reuse and recycling drives, plastic-free initiatives and creative utilisation of waste materials. Emphasis has also been placed on converting waste into useful and aesthetically meaningful products, promoting awareness on responsible waste management and reinforcing the message that waste can be transformed into a resource.
Documentation and Reporting
The activities undertaken across the ICAR network are being documented through daily photographs being uploaded on the SHS portal. Compiled daily reports along with photographs are being forwarded to DKMA for uploading on the ICAR website, facilitating regular documentation and dissemination of the campaign activities.
Culmination and Way Forward
The campaign will culminate on 1 October 2026 with participation in the nationwide “Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath” initiative through collective shramdaan and cleanliness activities, followed by the observance of Swachh Bharat Diwas on 2 October. The culmination will focus on showcasing transformed cleanliness target units and public spaces, undertaking appropriate cleanliness and shramdaan activities, promoting plantation and green spaces under “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam”, and recognising contributors, as appropriate. Through these activities, the ICAR system has sought to integrate cleanliness with public participation, youth engagement, environmental responsibility, dignity of sanitation workers and responsible waste management, while extending the message of Swachhata beyond institutional premises into communities and public spaces and reinforcing it as a sustained collective responsibility.

The Centre for Research on International Trade (CRIT), New Delhi, in partnership with the Indian Institute of Foreign Trade (IIFT), New Delhi, organised a three-day Orientation Course on Trade Negotiations from 28 to 30 September 2026 in New Delhi. The programme provided participants with an overview of key concepts, institutions and contemporary issues relating to international trade and trade negotiations.
The academic programme on the first day covered sessions on “Emerging World Trade Scenario: Challenges & Opportunities and Introduction to Basic Concepts of Trade Theory”, “Introduction to WTO” and a panel discussion on WTO issues.
The second day featured sessions on “Labour/Environment/Sustainability and Trade”, “Legal Analysis & Treaty Interpretation of Trade Agreements”, “Trade Analysis/Trade Databases” and “Dispute Settlement”.
On the third day, participants joined specialised tracks. Track I covered “Trade Remedies”, “Rules of Origin” and “Non-Tariff Measures (NTMs)”, while Track II covered “Intellectual Property Rights (IPR)”, “Digital Trade” and “Services”.
The programme concluded with the Valedictory Session, which included the valedictory address by Professor & Head, CTIL, with additional charge as Professor & Head, CWS, Dr. James J. Nedumpara ; the keynote address by Vice Chancellor, IIFT Dr. K. Rangarajan; and the Special Address by Additional Secretary, Department of Commerce, Shri Amitabh Kumar. Professor, CWS & Head Admin, CRIT, Dr. Murali Kallummal, proposed the vote of thanks, followed by the distribution of certificates.
In his Special Address, Shri Amitabh Kumar highlighted the role of trade in supporting GDP growth, while noting the need for trade professionals to navigate an increasingly complex global trading environment, including neo-mercantilist approaches and measures such as the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) and the European Union Deforestation Regulation (EUDR). Referring to India’s economic reforms since 1991 and its accession to the WTO in 1995, he highlighted the expanding scope of multilateral trade rules beyond goods to services, intellectual property rights and sustainability-related issues, and appreciated CRIT’s initiative in organising the capacity-building programme.
The three-day course provided participants with a structured understanding of the international trading system and trade negotiations, covering foundational concepts and the WTO framework, as well as the economic, legal and policy dimensions of contemporary trade. The specialised sessions further provided insights into key negotiating areas relevant to the evolving global trade landscape.

title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Participates in Opening Day of G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting in Milwauke, U.S
subtitle:
Shri Piyush Goyal Highlights India’s Food Security Measures and Reaffirms Commitment to Rules-Based Multilateral Trading System

G20 Trade Ministers Reach Consensus on Statement on Weaponization of Food through Coercive Trade Actions

Shri Piyush Goyal Holds Bilateral Meetings with Trade Ministers and Representatives of Key G20 Partners on Sidelines of G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 OCT 2026 7:59PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal participated in the opening day of the G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, hosted under the United States G20 Presidency.
Speaking at the session on food and trade, Shri Goyal thanked the Presidency for placing food at the centre of the discussions. He said that ensuring food security for all and creating greater opportunities for farmers are central to India’s policy and reiterated that food must never be used as an instrument of pressure against any country. He said that countries of the Global South are among the most adversely impacted by the food, fuel and fertiliser crises caused by global conflicts, and stressed that today’s fertiliser shortage could become tomorrow’s food crisis.
Shri Goyal said that during the COVID-19 pandemic, India ensured food security for over 1.4 billion citizens and supplied foodgrains to several countries in need. He noted that over 800 million people in India are currently being provided foodgrains free of cost.
The Minister said that India maintains public stockholding, procures from small and marginal farmers and, in the event of a harvest shortfall, adopts temporary and transparent measures to ensure the availability and affordability of food. He said these measures are recognised under the WTO, including through the Bali Ministerial Decision and the Geneva Ministerial Declaration. He called for a clear distinction between measures taken to ensure food security and coercive trade actions.
Shri Goyal also referred to existing mechanisms, including the G20 Agricultural Market Information System, established in 2011, and the exemption of purchases by the World Food Programme from export restrictions, adopted at the 12th Ministerial Conference of the WTO. He reaffirmed India’s commitment to a rules-based, fair, non-discriminatory, equitable, transparent, open, inclusive and multilateral trading system, with the WTO at its core.
The Ministers reached consensus on the outcome document, ‘G20 Statement on the Weaponization of Food through Coercive Trade Actions’, and expressed their intent to continue cooperation on the subject.
Earlier in the day, Shri Goyal joined G20 Trade Ministers and Ambassador Jamieson Greer, United States Trade Representative, on a visit to the Rockwell Automation office and factory in Mequon, Wisconsin.
On the sidelines of the Meeting, Shri Goyal held bilateral meetings with the Minister of Development, Industry, Trade and Services and the Foreign Minister of Brazil; the United States Trade Representative; the European Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security; the Secretary of State for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade and President of the Board of Trade of the United Kingdom; the Secretary of Economy of Mexico; and the Minister of Finance and Economy of the Republic of Poland.
The Minister also attended the welcome dinner hosted by Ambassador Greer and Secretary Rollins of the United States Department of Agriculture at the Milwaukee Art Museum.

title: Agreement Signed between DBN (Digital Bharat Nidhi) - Department of Telecommunications; Government of Maharashtra; MDIL; BSNL & MahaIT for Implementation of Amended BharatNet Program in Maharashtra
subtitle:
₹10,520 Crore Financial Support Approved for Rollout of Amended BharatNet Program in Maharashtra

Amended BharatNet Program in Maharashtra to Cover 28,237 Gram Panchayats and Provide On-Demand Connectivity to 15,799 Villages

Partnership to Strengthen and Upgrade Rural Telecom Infrastructure across Maharashtra
date:

                01 OCT 2026 7:44PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a significant step towards strengthening digital infrastructure and accelerating broadband connectivity across rural Maharashtra, Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN) under Department of Telecommunications (DoT) signed an Agreement for implementation of the Amended BharatNet Program (ABP) in the State under the State-led model today at Sanchar Bhawan, New Delhi.
The Agreement was signed between Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN), DoT; Government of Maharashtra; MahaNet Digital Infrastructure Limited (MDIL); Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) and Maharashtra Information Technology Corporation Limited (MahaIT) for implementation of the Amended BharatNet Program in the State of Maharashtra.
The Agreement signing ceremony was held in the august presence of Shri Shyamal Misra, Administrator, Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN); Shri Virendra Singh, Secretary, Department of Electronics, Information Technology & Artificial Intelligence, Government of Maharashtra; Smt. Buveneswari S., MD, Maharashtra Information Technology Corporation Limited (MahaIT); Shri Papa Sudhakara Rao, Director (Enterprise Business - EB), Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL); Shri Dinesh Kumar Garg, DDG (ABP Implementation-I), Department of Telecommunications, along with senior officers of DoT, DBN and BSNL.
The signing of the Agreement marks an important milestone towards expeditious implementation of the Program and reflects the shared commitment of the Central Government and the Government of Maharashtra towards strengthening rural digital infrastructure, enhancing last-mile connectivity and promoting inclusive digital growth.
The Union Cabinet had approved the Amended BharatNet Program on 4th August 2023 with the objective of upgrading, consolidating and expanding the existing BharatNet network to ensure robust and future-ready broadband connectivity to all Gram Panchayats and villages on demand basis.
Under the Amended BharatNet Program in Maharashtra, the project will be implemented through MahaNet Digital Infrastructure Limited (MDIL). The Program will have a total scope of 28,237 Gram Panchayats, which includes upgradation of 15,171 Phase I Gram Panchayats from linear to ring topology to enhance network resilience, coverage of 12,740 Phase II Gram Panchayats, and inclusion of 326 newly created Gram Panchayats. In addition, 15,799 villages will be provided connectivity on a demand basis to strengthen last-mile connectivity.
The Government of India has approved financial support of ₹10,520 crore for implementation of the Program in Maharashtra. The initiative is expected to facilitate more than nine lakh rural home fibre connections with financial support from the Government of India and significantly enhance delivery of digital services including e-Governance, online education, telemedicine, digital payments and citizen-centric services across rural and remote areas of the State.
The Agreement signed today is expected to accelerate execution of the Program in Maharashtra and further advance the vision of a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.
About Digital Bharat Nidhi
Digital Bharat Nidhi (erstwhile USOF) was established under the Indian Telegraph (Amendment) Act, 2003 w.e.f. 01.04.2002. As per ‘The Telecommunications Act, 2023’ the Universal Service Obligation Fund, has become the Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN). The DBN has mandate to support universal service through promoting access and delivery of telecommunication service in underserved rural, remote and urban areas. It is an attached office of the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications.
In order to achieve objectives of DBN, it covers various schemes and projects including BharatNet, 4G Saturation Project, Provision of Mobile Service in uncovered areas of Aspirational Districts, Mobile Services in Left Wing Extremist Areas, Mobile Services in Himalayan and Border areas, Mobile Services in Islands and Mobile Services in North Eastern Areas.

The Department of Posts has launched the implementation phase of Special Campaign 6, which will be undertaken from 2nd October to 31st October 2026 across its extensive nationwide network. The campaign is aimed at further institutionalising Swachhata, efficient record management, reduction of pendency and environmentally responsible waste management, with a special emphasis on the scientific management of e-waste and sustainable utilisation of departmental resources.
During Special Campaign 5, the Department covered 1.30 lakh campaign sites, disposed of 1,00,000 public grievances, reviewed and weeded out 17,352 files and e-files, freed 23,287 sq. ft. of office space and generated ₹1.02 crore through disposal of scrap and waste material.

Key Focus Areas of Special Campaign 6
Under Special Campaign 6, the Department of Posts has set the following targets:
Liquidation of pendency in public grievances and appeals – target for Special Campaign 6 is resolution of 1,50,000 grievances and 1500 appeals.
Cleanliness campaigns at 1,35,000 sites across the country.
These targets are intended to provide a focused and measurable framework for improving efficiency, cleanliness and responsiveness throughout the Department.
Swachhata: Taking the Last-Mile Approach
The Department of Posts is adopting a last-mile approach to Swachhata, extending its efforts beyond the physical cleanliness of Post Office premises to include clean processes, greater efficiency, accountability and a cultural reorientation among personnel.
The campaign covers all categories of Post Offices, including rural Branch Post Offices (BOs), with the objective of embedding cleanliness and efficient work practices into day-to-day functioning. The initiative seeks to strengthen citizen-centricity, responsive service delivery and the overall customer experience.

The objective is to go beyond aesthetic improvements and create Post Offices that are functional, accessible, customer-friendly and future-ready.

Further, SPA Post Offices are being renovated and modernised to upgrade existing facilities and promote uniform branding across the postal network. These initiatives are aimed at improving functionality, accessibility and the overall experience of customers visiting Post Offices.
Jan Sampark – Dak Chaupal
Under Special Campaign 6, the Department of Posts is organising Dak Chaupal to strengthen citizen engagement and bring Government services closer to the people. The initiative focuses on Digital India, financial inclusion and Antyodaya, with emphasis on last-mile delivery. Citizens are being sensitised about financial services, insurance, DBT, Payments Bank, e-commerce and export services, along with various Government welfare schemes and their benefits.

title: Government Revises Sugar Stock Holding Norms to Prevent Hoarding and Ensure Smooth Supply to Consumers During Festive Season
subtitle: Retail Sugar Prices Decline 15%; Ex-Mill Prices Down by Around 28%
ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 OCT 2026 12:54PM by PIB Delhi
content:
With the commencement of the new sugar season from 1st October, The Government of India has further strengthened measures to ensure adequate availability of sugar to consumers at reasonable prices during the festive season.
The Government has reduced the
stock holding period for sugar dealers to 15 days
and fixed the
stock holding limit at 1,000 quintals, with effect from 15 October 2026 to 30 November 2026
, except in Kolkata and its extended metropolitan areas and the State of Assam.
Under the revised provisions, with effect from 15 October 2026, a sugar dealer shall:
Not hold sugar stock for a period exceeding
15 days
from the date of receipt of such stock.
Not hold sugar stock exceeding
1,000 quintals
at any time and at any place across the country.
Considering the specific market requirements of the region, the stock holding limit has been fixed at
2,000 quintals for Kolkata and its extended metropolitan areas and the State of Assam
.
Kolkata sources sugar from Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Karnataka and supplies it to the eastern part of the country, including the North-Eastern region. The higher limit for Assam has been provided keeping in view geographical constraints, transportation logistics and consumer interest in the North-Eastern region.
The revised norms are aimed at ensuring that sugar is not unnecessarily accumulated in the distribution chain and that supplies move smoothly from sugar mills through dealers and ultimately reach the end consumer. The measure is particularly aimed at further curbing hoarding, discouraging speculative trading and preventing accumulation of sugar stocks by dealers. By limiting the quantity and duration for which sugar can be held, the Government seeks to facilitate an orderly movement of sugar through the supply chain and ensure its continuous availability to consumers at reasonable prices.
Retail Sugar Prices Decline by 15%
Average retail sugar prices have declined by
15 per cent from their August peak
and are expected to decline further as the benefit of lower ex-mill prices passes through the supply chain.
Ex-mill sugar prices have declined by approximately 28 per cent
and have remained stable over the last three weeks.
The decline reflects the impact of various measures taken by the Government to ensure adequate availability of sugar and facilitate its orderly movement through the market.
The Government has reiterated that sugar mills, dealers, wholesalers and other market participants are expected to ensure continuous movement of sugar through the supply chain and prevent artificial accumulation or speculative hoarding. Wholesalers and retailers have also been urged to immediately pass on the benefit of the substantial decline in ex-mill sugar prices to consumers.
Sugar mills have already been advised to commence crushing operations in accordance with the agro-climatic conditions prevailing in their respective regions. The Union Government will continue to monitor the impact of uneven and deficient rainfall associated with El Niño conditions on sugarcane in certain sugar-producing regions and take all necessary and timely measures to maintain a balance between domestic availability, consumer interest and the interests of sugarcane farmers.
Concerned State Governments have also been advised to take suitable action regarding crushing operations based on prevailing field conditions.
The Government reiterates that
sugarcane farmers and consumers are the two central pillars of India’s sugar policy
. While the Government remains committed to ensuring remunerative returns to sugarcane farmers, it is equally committed to protecting consumers from unreasonable increases in sugar prices and ensuring adequate availability of sugar across the country.

title: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code has strengthened credit discipline, improved recovery climate and contributed to ease of doing business: Harsh Malhotra, MoS, Corporate Affairs Ministry
subtitle: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) celebrates its Tenth Annual Day
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 OCT 2026 10:06PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Minister of State for Corporate Affairs Ministry and Road Transport and Highways, Shri Harsh Malhotra inaugurated the 10th Annual Day celebrations of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi today, marking ten years of IBBI since its establishment on 1st October, 2016.
Chief guest Shri Harsh Malhotra in his inaugural address, observed that the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC) has strengthened credit discipline, improved the recovery climate and contributed to the ease of doing business in the country. He noted the Government’s commitment to keep the Code responsive to emerging needs, including through the recent legislative amendments, and urged all stakeholders to work towards faster and value-maximising resolutions in the decade ahead.
MoS Shri Malhotra highlighted the need for improved adoption of emerging technologies, including AI, in IBC ecosystem. He noted that the efforts should be made towards faster resolutions and value maximisation as way forward.
Justice Shri Anupinder Singh Grewal, Hon’ble President, National Company Law Tribunal, reflected to the role of the Adjudicating Authority in the IBC framework. He highlighted the steps being taken to reduce delays in disposal of cases and recent improvements in speedier disposal of resolution plans. He noted various areas of reforms that may be considered in coming times including revision in admission thresholds, use of mediation, sector specific carveouts, etc.
Shri Indevar Pandey, Hon’ble Member, National Company Law Appellate Tribunal shared his perspective on the evolution of insolvency jurisprudence over the decade and the issues that may be considered in coming times. He highlighted that the IBC has seen seven sets of amendments to the Code in the last ten years. While noting the constraints involved in amending laws, he appreciated that amendments to the Code and regulations are being carried out in line with emerging needs in a timely manner. While noting the positive outcomes of IBC, he emphasised the need for timelines to be respected by all stakeholders.
Shri Ansuman Pattnaik, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, while noting the achievements of the IBC, highlighted the policy reforms undertaken to strengthen the Code, including the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Act, 2026. He noted key aspects of the amendment act and outlined the areas for the next phase of reforms in IBC framework and ecosystem.
Welcoming the guests, Shri Jayanti Prasad, Chairperson, IBBI, reflected on the ten-year journey of the Code and the Board. He noted that IBC has enabled substantial recoveries
for creditors, rescued viable businesses across sectors, and brought about a lasting change in
debtor–creditor behaviour. He observed that the ecosystem now comprises over 4,400 Insolvency Professionals and over 6,000 Registered Valuers, highlighting the responsive, participative and evidence-based approach to regulation-making being adopted by IBBI.
As part of the Tenth Annual Day celebrations, an annual publication, “Shaping the Next Decade of IBC: The Road Ahead”, was released during the event. On this occasion, winners of the 7th National Online Quiz on the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, were also felicitated.
The event was also graced by imminent dignitaries like Justice Shri Anupinder Singh Grewal, Hon’ble President, National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), Shri Indevar Pandey, Hon’ble Member, National Company Law Appellate Tribunal; and Shri Ansuman Pattnaik, Additional  Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs also honoured the occasion with their gracious presence. The event was also attended by Shri Jayanti Prasad, Chairperson, IBBI; Shri Sandip Garg, whole Time Member, IBBI; and Shri Bhushan Kumar Sinha, whole Time Member, IBBI. The event witnessed participation of eminent dignitaries and key stakeholders of the insolvency ecosystem.

title: Raksha Mantri Launches Key Digital and Financial Management Initiatives at Defence Accounts Department’s 279th Annual Day Celebration in New Delhi
subtitle:
“Maximum digitization, maximum automation, maximum transparency - this should be our goal.” said RM

“We must move from ‘annual review’ to ‘any time review’ of the budget, with real-time data enabling timely and informed decision-making.”

“Our approach must be firm, fair, sensitive and responsible, especially when dealing with the legitimate dues and service rights of those who have devoted their lives to defending the nation.”
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 OCT 2026 3:07PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh launched various publications and digital initiatives of the Defence Accounts Department (DAD) during the celebration of its 279th Annual Day at DRDO Bhawan, New Delhi on October 01, 2026. He congratulated DAD on its nearly three centuries of service to the nation and commended its contribution to defence financial audit and management , calling it the backbone of the country's defence preparedness.
During his address, Shri Rajnath Singh called for greater integration of financial systems of the Army, Navy and Air Force and stressed upon maximum digitisation, automation and transparency, with real-time updating of Management Information System data. RM urged the DAD to transition from “Annual Review of Balances” to “Any Time Review of Balances”.
Shri Rajnath Singh commended SAKSHAM, DAD’s project for digitising and integrating the Defence accounting and payment ecosystem hosted on a secure dedicated data centre and operating on the DAD WAN network. It uses the latest tech-stack with secure role-based access, enhanced validations and scalability, supporting the Department's move towards “One Nation, One Function, One Application”. RM appreciated it’s integration with the Indian Army Financial Information System for budget, approval and bill data.
Highlighting the near 100% expenditure during FY 2025–26, RM lauded the joint efforts of DAD and all three Services to achieve this milestone. Referring to the success of SPARSH data cleaning, RM suggested automating grievance redressal through a Conversational AI ecosystem covering chat, SMS, WhatsApp, email and phone calls. He also emphasised quality audit, digital data cleaning, and prompt resolution of grievances and court cases.“Our approach must be firm, fair, sensitive and responsible, especially when dealing with the legitimate dues and service rights of those who have devoted their lives to defending the nation,” said RM.
He stressed early implementation of SAMPURNA, a fully automated, end-to-end revenue procurement system envisaged to leverage data analytics, Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for a valuable decision-support system.
On the occasion, the Raksha Mantri unveiled three major initiatives aimed at strengthening the integration of Financial Information Systems of the Defence Forces, improving accounting and tracking of defence expenditure and operationalising the Treasury Single Account (TSA) system in the Ministry of Defence.
Integration of SAKSHAM with Indian Army Financial Information System
The SAKSHAM bill audit and payment system of the Defence Accounts Department has been successfully integrated with the Indian Army Financial Information System (IAFIS), facilitating digital transmission of budget, sanction and bill information between the two organisations. The integration is a major step towards complete digitisation of the Defence payments ecosystem, enabling real-time sharing of information on bill status and budget balances and completely paperless processing of bills.
Treasury Single Account System in Ministry of Defence
The Treasury Single Account (TSA) system in the Ministry of Defence was inaugurated by the Raksha Mantri for Just-In-Time release of funds to autonomous bodies under the Government of India. Operationalised through the Payment Routing and Integrated System Management (PRISM) platform, the system is fully integrated with RBI eKUBER. It will facilitate better grant management for autonomous bodies under the Ministry of Defence and provide greater visibility of accounting and expenditure.
Revamped National Compilation System
The Raksha Mantri launched the revamped National Compilation System (NCS) for Defence. The NCS is the single source for accounting and compilation of all Defence expenditure in India. The Ministry of Defence operates under a unique financial delegation framework, requiring budget allocation and expenditure tracking across various Controllers of the Defence Accounts Department across the country. The revamped NCS has been comprehensively redesigned on a new technical architecture to provide accurate budget reporting and expenditure monitoring. The system will facilitate granular reporting to the Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Defence, Service Headquarters and Field Controllers, thereby aiding policy planning and better budget management.
Raksha Mantri Awards for Excellence 2026
Raksha Mantri Awards for Excellence 2026 were presented during the event to recognise outstanding achievements by teams and individuals in implementing key reforms and projects. The awards recognise innovation, professionalism and efficiency in Defence financial management and contributions towards strengthening institutional capacity and enhancing transparency in the Department’s service to the Defence Forces.
The awards acknowledged the significant role played by DAD officials across the country in successful digitization of Annual Review of Balances (ARoB) and implementation of various initiatives, including SAKSHAM & SAMAR-SETU.
SAMAR-SETU is a centralised application for management of pay and allowances of Agniveers of the Indian Army. Operating from the Central Agniveer Pay and Accounts Office (CAPAO), the system manages the pay accounts of more than 2.3 lakh Agniveers through fully system-driven automated processes.
Raksha Mantri released three publications during DAD Day 2026 including the Comprehensive Statistical Handbook on Defence Expenditure (COSHE) 2026, Raksha Lekha Bharati and the Market Intelligence Report 2025-2026. A film showcasing the success of the System for Pension Administration (Raksha), SPARSH, was also screened.
Addressing the gathering, Controller General of Defence Accounts (CGDA) Smt Alka Nangia Arora highlighted the important initiatives undertaken by the Defence Accounts Department in current year, including major strides in the centralisation and digitisation of its core functions of internal audit, payment and accounting, financial advice and management of Defence pensions.
Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani, Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, Chief of Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth, Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary (Defence Finance) Shri Vishvajit Sahay, and Vice Chief of Air Staff Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit were also in attendance, along with senior officials from the Ministry of Defence.
Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani, Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, Chief of Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth, Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary (ESW), Smt Sukriti Likhi, Secretary (Defence Finance) Shri Vishvajit Sahay, and Vice Chief of Air Staff Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit were also in attendance, along with senior officials from the Ministry of Defence.

content:
The Union Ministry of Education has extended the last date for submission of applications under the National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) for the academic year 2026-27 to
October 31, 2026
. The extension will provide eligible students additional time to complete their applications on the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) and facilitate timely verification by the concerned authorities.

Process

November 15, 2026
