Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia to deliver keynote address on ‘Connected India, Empowered Finance: Building Trusted Digital Infrastructure for the AI Economy

Union Cabinet Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat will deliver the keynote address on Culture as Capital: From Heritage to Horizons

Over 200 Indian and international participants from around 30 countries to discuss resilience, global fragmentation, technology, trade, finance and India’s economic priorities
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 OCT 2026 2:31PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave (KEC 2026) is scheduled to be held from 3rd to 5th October 2026 at New Delhi, under the theme “Resilience in an Age of Flux”. The three-day gathering will bring together senior policymakers, economists, academics, financial experts and international thought leaders.
The 5th edition of KEC will bring together more than 180 policymakers, economists, academics, financial experts and international thought leaders, including over 80 international participants from around 30 countries. They will contribute to the Conclave’s plenary sessions, interactive discussions and focused roundtables.
The Institute of Economic Growth (IEG) was founded by Professor V.K.R.V. Rao in 1952. Currently, Shri N. K. Singh is the President, Board of Trustees, IEG. Dr. Michael Debabrata Patra is Chairman of the Board of Governors, and Professor Sabyasachi Kar is Director of the Institute.
The Kautilya Economic Conclave is an initiative of the Institute of Economic Growth (IEG), organised in partnership with the Ministry of Finance, Government of India. First convened in 2022, the Conclave provides a forum for dialogue on contemporary economic and policy challenges.
Since its inception in 2022, the Kautilya Economic Conclave has grown into a forum for dialogue on economic and policy challenges. Earlier editions were held under the themes “Redefining the Future” (2022), “Navigating a World on Fire” (2023), “The Indian Era” (2024) and “Seeking Prosperity in Turbulent Times” (2025).
Vice President of India Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan will deliver the inaugural address
on October 3, 2026. The inaugural session will examine how economic policy can build resilience without sacrificing growth, openness or institutional credibility in an environment marked by recurrent global shocks and uncertainty.
A special plenary on
“Resilience in an Age of Flux: India’s Economic Priorities”
will focus on how India can sustain growth, preserve macroeconomic stability and expand investment amid global fragmentation, technological disruption and recurrent shocks.
Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman
will deliver the special address
, with Amelie de Montchalin, President of the Cour des Comptes and former Minister of Public Action and Accounts of France, as discussant.
The concluding session,
“India and the World: Adaptive by Design”
, will be moderated by Shri N. K. Singh, President, Board of Trustees, Institute of Economic Growth.
Dr. S. Jaishankar, Union Minister for External Affairs, will deliver the special concluding address
, with former Singapore Foreign Minister Mr. George Yeo as discussant. The session will examine how India can remain adaptive by design, preserve strategic autonomy, widen partnerships and respond flexibly to a more contested and uncertain global order.
Technology and the digital economy will constitute another major strand of KEC 2026.
Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, will deliver the keynote address
at the plenary on “
Connected India, Empowered Finance: Building Trusted Digital Infrastructure for the AI Economy”
. The session will examine how digital infrastructure, artificial intelligence and new communications networks can raise productivity while preserving competition and trust.
Union Cabinet Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat
will deliver the keynote address on Culture as Capital: From Heritage to Horizons on the penultimate day.
The opening plenary,
“A World Priced for Risk”
, will examine how energy shocks, supply-chain disruptions and the weaponisation of trade and economic access are creating renewed challenges for macroeconomic management, investment and resilience. The session will be chaired by Lord Nicholas Stern, with Shri P. K. Mishra, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, delivering the keynote address and Professor Michael Greenstone of the University of Chicago as discussant.
The Conclave will also feature Shri Shaktikanta Das, Principal Secretary-2 to the Prime Minister and former Governor of the Reserve Bank of India, as keynote speaker in the plenary session
“Kautilya and a Resurgent India: Lessons for Emerging Markets”
. The session will explore the lessons that India’s economic experience can offer emerging markets and will feature José De Gregorio, former President of the Central Bank of Chile, and Muhamad Chatib Basri, former Finance Minister of Indonesia.
The role of central banks in navigating a more volatile global environment will be a key focus of the Conclave. In the plenary session
“Central Banking in an Age of Flux”
,
Shri Sanjay Malhotra, Governor of the Reserve Bank of India, will deliver the special address
. Chaired by Jean-Claude Trichet, former President of the European Central Bank and former Governor of the Banque de France, the session will consider how central banks can manage inflation, financial fragility, capital flows and credibility amid recurrent global shocks. Governor Malhotra’s participation will provide an important perspective on the challenges confronting monetary policy and financial stability in a rapidly changing global economy.
The agenda will address a wide range of domestic and global economic issues, including fiscal federalism, industrial policy, capital-market development, regulatory oversight, development finance and the mobilisation of domestic and foreign capital for long-term investment. Sessions will examine the institutional and fiscal principles governing Centre-State relations, the role of industrial policy in structural transformation, and the conditions required to deepen India’s capital markets and channel savings into productive risk capital.
International perspectives will form an important part of the Conclave. Sessions will examine Europe’s growth and competitiveness challenges and its economic relationship with Asia; global imbalances, debt and financial stability; structural transformation in China; and Japan’s role in economic security, technology and connectivity in the Indo-Pacific.
A dedicated plenary,
“Balancing Contradictions in the Age of Flux”
, will consider how India can manage competing strategic and economic relationships while preserving strategic autonomy, economic interests and room for manoeuvre. The discussion will bring together international experts on Asia, China, Taiwan and India’s global economic relationships.
Parallel sessions will further explore
“The New Tech Order: Power, Platforms, AI and Regulatory Competition”
and
“Humans and Machines: Work, Skills and Education in the AI Age”
. These discussions will focus on how artificial intelligence and strategic technologies are reshaping economic power, labour markets, skills, education and regulatory frameworks.
Other sessions will address climate resilience, reform of multilateral development banks, healthcare and global health security, urbanisation, agriculture, demographic change and the future of work. Discussions on
“Feeding the Future”
will examine the resilience of agriculture and food systems amid climate uncertainty and trade disruptions, while
“Demography at a Turning Point”
will consider the implications of ageing, fertility, migration and demographic change for labour markets and productivity.
The Conclave will also examine the transformation of global trade and investment networks. A plenary on
“From Globalisation to Fragmentation: Rewiring Trade Networks”
will consider how strategic rivalry, industrial policy and economic security are reshaping trade, investment and supply chains. Another session,
“The New Growth Corridor: Reimagining Asia-Africa Economic Partnerships”
, will focus on opportunities for deeper trade, investment, infrastructure and development partnerships between Asia and Africa.
The three-day Conclave will feature plenary sessions, interactive parallel sessions and invitation-only closed-door roundtables. The roundtables will focus on issues including attracting foreign direct investment and mobilising domestic capital for long-term investment, providing opportunities for more focused exchanges among policymakers, economists, investors and practitioners. The Conclave is a “by invitation only” event.

title: Union Ministry of Health & Family Welfare Organises National Workshop to Strengthen Implementation of PC&PNDT Act
subtitle:
PC&PNDT Act Enforcement Must Go Hand-in-Hand with Sustained IEC to Promote the Equal Value of Girl Child: Smt. Aradhana Patnaik, Additional Secretary & Mission Director (NHM)

National Sex Ratio at Birth Rises from 898 to 918 Females per 1,000 Males: AS & MD, NHM

Workshop brings together representatives from all States and UTs to strengthen regulatory compliance, digital governance and enforcement against sex selection
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 OCT 2026 5:22PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, today organised a National Workshop on Strengthening the Implementation of the Pre-conception and Pre-natal Diagnostic Techniques (Prohibition of Sex Selection) Act, 1994 (PC&PNDT Act) in the national capital. The workshop brought together representatives from all 36 States and Union Territories, along with senior officials of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs.
The workshop focused on strengthening regulatory compliance, enhancing digital governance and ease of doing business, addressing emerging challenges in the digital ecosystem, and sharing State-level best practices to improve implementation of the PC&PNDT Act.
Delivering the keynote address, Smt. Aradhana Patnaik, Additional Secretary & Mission Director (NHM), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, emphasised the need for strict and effective enforcement of the PC&PNDT Act, complemented by sustained Information, Education and Communication (IEC) initiatives to reinforce the equal value of the girl child.
Highlighting the opportunities and challenges arising from emerging technologies, Ms. Patnaik noted that portable diagnostic devices, online platforms and social media have significantly expanded access to healthcare and information, but can also be misused for activities prohibited under the law. She stressed that technology must be leveraged to advance healthcare and social inclusion and must not be allowed to facilitate sex selection or gender discrimination.
Highlighting the progress made in improving the Sex Ratio at Birth (SRB), Ms. Patnaik noted that the national SRB has shown a steady improvement over the years. As per the Sample Registration System (SRS) Report 2024, the national SRB increased by 20 points, from 898 females per 1,000 males during 2014–16 to 918 females per 1,000 males during 2022–24. The improvement reflects the continued efforts towards effective implementation of the PC&PNDT Act, regulatory oversight and community-level interventions.
The workshop also deliberated on emerging challenges associated with the digital ecosystem, particularly online advertisements and content relating to sex selection and sex determination.
A dedicated session on Section 22 of the PC&PNDT Act highlighted the role of States and Union Territories in identifying, flagging and restricting prohibited digital content. The discussions also covered the use of the Sahyog Portal and the need for proactive coordination with digital intermediaries to address online violations and prevent misuse of technology for activities prohibited under the Act.
Deliberations were also held on standardising and strengthening State/UT PC&PNDT portals. The discussions focused on integrating digital modules for regulatory processes, monitoring and compliance to strengthen oversight while facilitating ease of doing business. Live demonstrations of digital initiatives undertaken by Telangana and Gujarat provided practical insights and enabled participating States and UTs to examine replicable models for strengthening digital governance under the PC&PNDT framework.
The workshop also provided a platform for States and UTs to share their experiences and innovative practices. Representatives from Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Haryana, Jharkhand, Odisha and Tamil Nadu, among others, presented State-level initiatives and best practices. The exchange facilitated peer learning and discussions on actionable measures to further strengthen implementation of the PC&PNDT Act.
Ms. Meera Srivastava, Joint Secretary (RCH), MoHFW; Dr. Pawan Kumar, Additional Commissioner (PC&PNDT), MoHFW; senior officials from the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs; and senior officials from all States and Union Territories were present during the workshop.

title: National Voluntary Blood Donation Day 2026 Observed with Renewed Call for Regular Voluntary Blood Donation
subtitle:
Dr. M. Srinivas Calls for Concerted Efforts to Strengthen Voluntary Blood Donation and Promote Optimal Use of Blood Components

State Blood Transfusion Councils, NGOs and Organisations Felicitated for Contribution towards Promotion of Voluntary Blood Donation
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 OCT 2026 2:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
National Voluntary Blood Donation Day (NVBDD) 2026 was observed today at Swarn Jayanti Auditorium, Lady Hardinge Medical College (LHMC), New Delhi, with a renewed emphasis on strengthening the culture of regular, voluntary and non-remunerated blood donation to ensure a safe, adequate and sustainable supply of blood and blood components across the country.
The national observance was organised by the Blood Transfusion Services (BTS) Division, Directorate General of Health Services (Dte. GHS), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India, in collaboration with Lady Hardinge Medical College and Associated Hospitals, New Delhi. The theme of NVBDD 2026 was
“One Drop of Humanity. Give Blood. Save Lives.”
Dr. M. Srinivas, Member (Health), NITI Aayog, presided over the programme and inaugurated the voluntary blood donation camp organised as part of the observance. The programme was attended by Dr. Loveneesh G. Krishna, Director General of Health Services (DGHS); Dr. Himani Ahluwalia, Director, LHMC and Associated Hospitals; senior officials of Health Services; experts in Transfusion Medicine; healthcare professionals; representatives of State Blood Transfusion Councils, blood centres, voluntary organisations and educational institutions; and voluntary blood donors.
The programme commenced with the inauguration of the voluntary blood donation camp. This was followed by a Nukkad Natak and cultural performances by students of Lady Hardinge Medical College to disseminate the message of voluntary blood donation and highlight its importance in saving lives. The programme also included administration of the voluntary blood donation pledge, addresses by dignitaries and felicitation of States, organisations and stakeholders for their contribution towards promotion of voluntary blood donation. The programme concluded with the singing of the National Song followed by the National Anthem.
Addressing the gathering, Dr. M. Srinivas highlighted the importance of voluntary blood donation in ensuring an adequate and sustainable blood supply and emphasised the collective responsibility of citizens and stakeholders in strengthening voluntary blood donation.
Dr. Srinivas administered the voluntary blood donation pledge at the outset of his address and called upon citizens not only to donate blood regularly but also to create awareness and encourage greater participation in voluntary blood donation within their communities.
Acknowledging the contribution of blood donation organisations and volunteers towards the nation and humanity, Dr. Srinivas noted that around 75 per cent of blood collection in the country is through voluntary donation. He called for concerted efforts by the Government, healthcare professionals, NGOs, voluntary organisations and youth organisations to further expand voluntary blood donation and address gaps between demand and availability.
He also underscored the importance of rational and optimal utilisation of blood and its components. He called for expanding awareness on blood health beyond blood donation to include related issues such as nutrition and anaemia, particularly among women and adolescent girls.
Dr. Srinivas urged healthcare institutions, voluntary organisations and community groups to take these messages to the grassroots and contribute towards strengthening public awareness about the importance of blood, blood components and voluntary blood donation.
Dr. Loveneesh G. Krishna, Director General of Health Services, acknowledged the contribution of voluntary blood donors, institutions and organisations engaged in strengthening blood transfusion services across the country.
He highlighted various measures undertaken by the Directorate General of Health Services, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, for strengthening blood transfusion services, including implementation of the National Blood Policy, strengthening of quality assurance and quality management practices, utilisation of the e-RaktKosh portal for donor registration and monitoring, development of national technical guidelines and implementation of Information, Education and Communication (IEC) initiatives.
Dr. Krishna emphasised that systems and infrastructure, while essential, need to be complemented by sustained voluntary participation to ensure adequate availability of blood. He called for strengthening a culture of regular, voluntary and non-remunerated blood donation, with particular emphasis on greater participation of youth.
Highlighting the human dimension of blood donation, Dr. Krishna observed that behind every unit of blood is a patient, behind every patient is a family, and behind every donor is an act of humanity. He called upon all stakeholders to contribute towards strengthening voluntary blood donation and make it an integral part of responsible citizenship.
LHMC Reaffirms Commitment to Safe and Quality Blood Services
Dr. Himani Ahluwalia, Director, LHMC and Associated Hospitals, highlighted the institution’s commitment to its core values of service, education and community responsibility and reaffirmed LHMC’s commitment to ensuring access to safe and quality blood services.
She stated that LHMC provides free treatment and transfusion support to around 700 registered thalassemia patients, making it one of the largest such services among government hospitals in the country.
Dr. Ahluwalia further highlighted the various initiatives undertaken by LHMC to promote voluntary blood donation, including regular voluntary blood donation camps, awareness campaigns, street plays and other community outreach activities.
States Recognised for Performance in Blood Collection during 2025
State Blood Transfusion Councils were felicitated during the national observance in recognition of their performance in blood collection during 2025 and their contribution towards strengthening voluntary blood donation.
Among the North-Eastern States,
Mizoram secured the first position, followed by Sikkim in the second position
.
Among the Union Territories,
Chandigarh secured the first position, followed by Delhi in the second position
.
Among the remaining States,
Haryana secured the first position, Uttarakhand the second position and Punjab the third position
.
The recognition acknowledges the sustained efforts of State Blood Transfusion Councils towards donor mobilisation, expansion of voluntary donor participation and promotion of voluntary blood donation.
NGOs and organisations making significant contributions towards promotion of voluntary blood donation and strengthening blood transfusion services were also felicitated. These included
Thalassaemics India; Akhil Bharatiya Terapanth Yuvak Parishad (ABTYP); All India Radio; and Indian Red Cross Society
, among others.
Nationwide Mega Voluntary Blood Donation Campaign
The national observance forms part of the
Nationwide Mega Voluntary Blood Donation Campaign
, being conducted from
17 September to 2 October 2026
across the country.
The campaign seeks to promote regular voluntary blood donation, strengthen the voluntary donor base and facilitate wider participation of citizens, institutions and communities. State and Union Territory Health Departments, State Blood Transfusion Councils, blood centres, healthcare and educational institutions, government departments, voluntary organisations and community groups are participating in the campaign.
The campaign places particular emphasis on youth participation, grassroots outreach, awareness generation and Jan Bhagidari. The
e-RaktKosh portal
is being utilised for donor registration and monitoring of blood collection activities. The voluntary blood donation pledge is also being promoted through digital platforms, including MyGov, to facilitate wider citizen participation.
Voluntary Blood Donation: An Essential Public Health Responsibility
National Voluntary Blood Donation Day is observed on
1st October every year
to generate awareness about the importance of voluntary blood donation and encourage healthy and eligible individuals to donate blood regularly.
Blood and blood components are required for a wide range of medical interventions, including surgery, trauma care, management of severe anaemia, cancer and blood disorders, maternal care and other life-saving procedures. As blood cannot be manufactured, its availability is dependent upon the voluntary participation of eligible donors.
Regular voluntary blood donation is therefore an important contribution towards ensuring timely availability of blood and blood components for patients in need.
The theme of NVBDD 2026,
“One Drop of Humanity. Give Blood. Save Lives.”
, underscores the humanitarian spirit of voluntary blood donation and calls upon eligible citizens, particularly youth, to contribute towards this life-saving cause.
The observance concluded with an appeal to citizens, healthcare institutions, educational institutions, government departments, voluntary organisations and other stakeholders to sustain efforts towards regular, voluntary and non-remunerated blood donation throughout the year.
The
Nationwide Mega Voluntary Blood Donation Campaign
will continue up to
2 October 2026
, with participating States, Union Territories, blood centres and organisations undertaking blood donation drives, donor mobilisation and awareness activities to further strengthen the culture of voluntary blood donation across the country.

title: Union Jal Shakti Minister Shri C. R. Paatil Hosts Water Warriors from Across India at His Residence
subtitle:
Grassroots champions share inspiring stories of river rejuvenation, water conservation and community mobilization

Shri Paatil calls for focused action, measurable outcomes and wider Jan Bhagidari

Secretary, DoWR, RD & GR Smt. Archana Varma lauds their role in mobilising communities for collective action on water
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 OCT 2026 6:42PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Jal Shakti Shri C. R. Paatil today interacted with Water Conservation Warriors and River Rejuvenation Warriors from different parts of the country who have been leading grassroots initiatives in water conservation, river and water-body rejuvenation and environmental protection. The interaction, organised by the National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG) under Namami Gange, provided a platform for these grassroots champions to share their journeys, learn from one another and discuss how successful community-led models can be strengthened and replicated across the country.
The participants shared first-hand experiences of restoring rivers and ponds, undertaking Shramdaan, promoting rainwater harvesting, removing plastic and other waste near water bodies, carrying out plantation drives and mobilising women, youth, volunteers and local communities. Their stories highlighted how individual initiative, when combined with collective action and community ownership, can translate into visible and sustained improvements on the ground.
Among those who shared their work was
Ramveer Tanwar
, popularly known as the ‘Pondman of India’, who spoke about rejuvenating more than 100 ponds and establishing 10 mini urban forests.
Kamini Kumari
from Bihar highlighted her initiative in mobilising 500 women to construct 500 groundwater recharge pits along the Baya River in a single day, linking water conservation with groundwater recharge, sustainable agriculture and livelihood opportunities for women.
Surendra Singh Chaudhary
, popularly known as ‘Bittu Tabahi’, shared his journey of taking up the clean-up of the polluted Ajnar River at Biaora in Rajgarh district of Madhya Pradesh. A young B.Sc. student, he began the effort on 26 January 2026 and undertook hands-on removal of plastic, weeds, sludge and other waste from the river, largely through his own initiative. His work, which began as a local effort, drew wider public attention and has inspired greater participation in the cleaning and restoration of local water bodies.
Anand Malligavad
from Bengaluru spoke about his work in restoring 33 lakes and planting more than one lakh native trees. Jagdish Singh Negi from Uttarakhand shared his work in water conservation, forest restoration and converting plastic waste into eco-bricks.
Subham Kumar
highlighted the role of youth and volunteers in river cleanliness and his efforts to mobilise communities to remove more than 2.47 lakh kilograms of waste from the banks of the Ganga and its tributaries.
The interaction also highlighted the role of water volunteers and community groups in sustaining clean rivers and ghats
. Akash Yadav
from Uttar Pradesh shared how his 15-member volunteer group has contributed to the rejuvenation of four Ganga ghats and the removal of more than one tonne of plastic waste.
Dr. Sanjivini Sharma
from Kanpur spoke about mobilising more than 900 volunteers for Ganga conservation campaigns and removing over 120 metric tonnes of waste, besides promoting plastic recycling, reuse of discarded materials and livelihood opportunities for women through community-led waste management.
The other water warriors included Ms. Kusum Gildiyal, Sh. Jagdish Negi, Ms. Rama Tiwari, Dr. Suman Pandey, Ms. Kumari Sunita Singh, Sh. Sanjay Kumar Singh, Sh. Ajay Kumar Tivare, Sh. Nitish Kumar Singh, Sh. Kamlesh Bhai Shastri, Sh. Sandeep Chaudhary, Ms. Sirkunwar, Ms. Phoolbati and Sh. Vivek Bhat. The work of these warriors were highly appreciated by Hon’ble Minister Jal Shakti.
Addressing the gathering, Smt. Archana Varma, Secretary, Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, appreciated the role played by the Water Warriors in taking the message of water conservation and cleanliness beyond government programmes and into communities. She praised their ability to bring people together and mobilise collective action around rivers, ponds and other water bodies, and emphasised that such citizen-led participation is essential for sustaining water conservation and river rejuvenation efforts over the long term.
Addressing the participants, Shri C. R. Paatil congratulated them for their commitment and said that listening directly to their experiences was an opportunity to understand the scale, diversity and impact of grassroots action taking place across the country. He acknowledged that many of them had worked through difficult local circumstances and had nevertheless succeeded in bringing people together for the protection of water and the environment. Referring to the larger national movement, Shri Paatil said that under the visionary leadership of Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, water conservation has evolved into a nationwide Jan Andolan anchored in Jan Bhagidari. He said that the Prime Minister's consistent emphasis on conserving every drop of water has inspired citizens and communities across the country to take ownership of water conservation, and that the work of the Water Warriors and reflects this spirit of collective action.
The Minister emphasized that the next step should be to translate this energy into focused, measurable and sustained outcomes. He encouraged the participants to identify specific rivers, ponds, ghats and other water bodies, set clear targets and demonstrate visible improvement on the ground. He also stressed the importance of involving women, youth, schoolchildren, senior citizens and other sections of society so that water conservation and cleanliness become enduring people’s movements rather than one-time activities.
Shri Paatil encouraged the Water Warriors to remain connected with one another, regularly share their work and learn from successful models being implemented in different parts of the country. He said that good local initiatives should not remain confined to one place, but should be adapted and expanded wherever they can help communities address similar challenges.
The Water Warriors expressed happiness at being invited by the Minister to his residence and at the opportunity to share their stories directly with him. They also valued the chance to interact with fellow grassroots champions from different parts of India, exchange experiences, understand different approaches to community mobilisation and explore ways to remain connected and collaborate in future.
The interaction reaffirmed that protecting rivers and conserving water cannot be achieved through infrastructure and government programmes alone. Sustained Jan Bhagidari, Shramdaan, responsible community behaviour and committed grassroots leadership are equally important. The experiences shared during the meeting demonstrated how citizens, volunteers and local communities can become powerful partners in the national effort for clean rivers, conserved water resources and a cleaner, more sustainable environment.

The Ministry of Jal Shakti, under the leadership of the Union Minister for Jal Shakti, Shri C R Patil and Minister of State,
Shri V. Somanna
, organized a large-scale Shramdaan activity today at 7:30 AM at Kalindi Kunj Ghat, Okhla Barrage in New Delhi as part of the nationwide campaign for Shramdaan activity under Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026-Nirantar Prayas.

The minister also urged the citizens to make Swachhata a collective responsibility by ensuring cleanliness in their surroundings. title: DDWS Organizes Second Follow-up Meeting to accelerate drinking water coverage in tribal areas under PM-JANMAN and DA-JGUA
subtitle: States and UTs urged to harmonize data, identify left-out habitations and submit validated proposals in a time-bound manner
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 OCT 2026 11:27AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, convened the second follow-up review and convergence meeting yesterday to accelerate saturation of drinking water coverage in tribal areas under the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) and Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA-JGUA). The meeting was chaired by the Secretary, DDWS and attended by senior officials of the National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA), State Rural Water Supply/Public Health Engineering Departments, State Tribal Welfare Departments and other concerned stakeholders.
The meeting was held as part of the follow-up process initiated after the Departmental Summit, where States and Union Territories had committed to achieving saturation of drinking water coverage in all eligible PM-JANMAN and DA-JGUA villages. Progress on these commitments was reviewed and States were advised to translate the commitments into time-bound action through closer coordination between Water Supply/PHE and Tribal Welfare Departments, ensuring that no eligible tribal village or habitation remains left out.
A dedicated provision of ₹5,000 crore under JJM 2.0 has been earmarked to address drinking water gaps in PM-JANMAN and DA-JGUA villages. In this context, the review focused on four priority areas: harmonisation of data between Tribal Welfare Departments and JJM databases, identification of uncovered villages and habitations, preparation of technically sound proposals and joint validation and certification of coverage. States and UTs were urged to complete these activities expeditiously and submit validated proposals for consideration.
Addressing the participants, Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS emphasised that regular reviews of PM-JANMAN and DA-JGUA villages should be undertaken through District Water and Sanitation Mission (DWSM) meetings chaired by the Deputy Commissioner/District Magistrate. He underscored that the DWSM should serve as the principal platform for inter-departmental coordination, validation of survey findings and identification of genuine coverage gaps requiring intervention.
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs has undertaken a State-wise
SurveySetu
exercise, including household-level verification of Functional Household Tap Connection (FHTC) status. States were advised to present SurveySetu findings jointly before the DWSM through representatives of Water Supply Departments, Tribal Welfare Departments and the survey agency. Any discrepancies identified during the exercise are to be resolved through consultation and field verification, wherever required, so that a final validated database is available at the district level.
The meeting reiterated that the objective is not only to create new infrastructure but to achieve complete saturation and certification of all eligible PM-JANMAN and DA-JGUA villages. States were therefore advised to accord equal priority to certification of villages that have already achieved saturation and ensure that all eligible settlements are accurately reflected in the JJM-IMIS before submission of proposals.
States and UTs were advised to identify left-out habitations based on SurveySetu findings and validate them through the DWSM mechanism. The Rural Water Supply/PHE and Tribal Welfare Departments have been asked to jointly prepare proposals supported by self-assessed DPR Checklists duly authenticated by competent authorities. Proposals should clearly establish the justification for inclusion, avoid duplication, incorporate validated LGD codes and contain complete technical and financial details.
The Technical Division of NJJM also emphasised the need to improve the quality and completeness of DPR submissions. States were advised to ensure realistic population projections, adherence to prescribed service levels, adequate provisions for source sustainability and water security, and reasonable per-FHTC costs supported by appropriate technical justification. Particular attention was drawn towards accurate completion of DPR Checklists and proper authentication of all corrections and revisions.
Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, AS&MD, NJJM
said that the importance of joint ownership at the State level was also reiterated. State RWS/PHE and Tribal Welfare Departments will jointly prepare and present proposals before the Joint Committee co-chaired by the Secretary, DDWS and Secretary, MoTA. At the district level, the DWSM chaired by the DC/DM will serve as the key platform for validation and decision-making, with participation of the survey agency and concerned State departments.
During the meeting, State-wise progress and observations on proposals already received were reviewed. Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Jharkhand, Kerala and Manipur were advised to address specific observations relating to LGD code validation, DPR documentation, service levels and per-FHTC costs. Bihar, Tamil Nadu and Assam were requested to take action on observations already communicated by DDWS. Several States also shared timelines for submission of proposals, with Ladakh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh indicating that proposals covering identified PM-JANMAN and DA-JGUA villages would be submitted during October 2026.
As part of the agreed way forward, States and UTs will establish a common validated database through harmonisation of PM-JANMAN, DA-JGUA, SurveySetu and JJM-IMIS records. Jointly validated proposals, along with duly signed DPR Checklists and requisite approvals, will be submitted for consideration by the Joint Committee co-chaired by the Secretary, DDWS and Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs. District administrations have also been advised to validate SurveySetu findings through DWSM meetings and communicate any additions or deletions identified during district-level verification to the State Government and DDWS.
The meeting reaffirmed the collective commitment of DDWS, MoTA, State Water Supply/PHE Departments, Tribal Welfare Departments and district administrations towards ensuring saturation of functional drinking water services in all eligible PM-JANMAN and DA-JGUA villages. Through data harmonisation, district-level validation, joint planning, timely submission of proposals and certification of saturation, the initiative aims to ensure that every eligible tribal village and habitation is provided with reliable and sustainable drinking water services.

Media professionals play a vital role in amplifying the reach and visibility of IFFI each year. Through news reports, interviews, reviews, features and digital coverage, the media helps bring the festival’s films, events and conversations to audiences across India and around the world. It helps celebrate diverse artists and their art. IFFI values the continued participation of the media in the festival which is instrumental in creating wider awareness and building public engagement with IFFI and with creative expression.

, and

, and attended by around 90 participants, including representatives of industry associations and business establishments, employers, industrialists and professionals.

, provided an overview of the four Labour Codes and the employer compliance chain.

, and witnessed participation of around 200 stakeholders, including representatives of the

.

, the Ministry, in collaboration with the

title: Special Gram Sabhas across India to Mark 2nd October with Discussions on Transformative Governance Reforms ; Launch People’s Plan Campaign 2026-27  ‘Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas’
subtitle: Several Ministries/Departments to place Citizen-Centric Schemes and Initiatives at the Centre of Gram Sabha Discussions
date:

                01 OCT 2026 12:52PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Special Gram Sabhas across the country will assemble on 2nd October 2026 to discuss transformative governance reforms and initiatives that are strengthening Panchayats, improving public services and enhancing the quality of life in rural India. These special Gram Sabhas will also mark the launch of the People’s Plan Campaign (PPC) 2026-27, “Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas”, under which Gram Panchayats will prepare their Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) for Financial Year 2027-28 through participatory and evidence-based planning. The Gram Sabha discussions will bring together citizens and local representatives to review the benefits and implementation of key Government schemes and initiatives, identify local needs and gaps and deliberate on priorities for the development of their villages.
The Ministry of Panchayati Raj, in collaboration with participating Ministries and Departments, Government of India is facilitating these discussions as part of a Whole-of-Government approach to grassroots development. The following schemes and initiatives will be highlighted during the Special Gram Sabhas:
Ministry of Panchayati Raj: Strengthening Panchayats through Finance Commission grants, capacity building under the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan, digital governance through eGramSwaraj and AuditOnline, Own Source Revenue (OSR) initiatives, SVAMITVA and the Panchayat Advancement Index.
Department of Rural Development: The Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G), providing a statutory guarantee of 125 days of wage employment, along with the Viksit Gram Panchayat Plan for locally determined works and livelihoods.
Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation: Jal Jeevan Mission for rural household tap water connections and Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) for sanitation, ODF Plus and solid and liquid waste management.
Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation: Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain and revised watershed development norms to strengthen groundwater recharge, water conservation and water security.
Department of Food and Public Distribution: One Nation One Ration Card for portability of foodgrain entitlements and Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana for continued food security.
Department of Consumer Affairs: National Consumer Helpline and e-Jagriti to strengthen consumer awareness, grievance redressal and access to consumer justice.
Department of Land Resources: The Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP) for digitised and accessible land records, supporting secure property rights and easier access to credit and watershed development under Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana.
The People’s Plan Campaign has been implemented across States and Union Territories since 2018, enabling Panchayats to prepare holistic, inclusive and participatory development plans. More than 2.55 lakh Gram Panchayats prepare and upload their plans on eGramSwaraj. The Panchayat Advancement Index enables Panchayats to identify achievements and gaps across key areas of local development, providing a basis for the Gram Sabha to identify priorities and take a Sankalp for the year ahead. The Gram Sabha provides citizens with a direct platform to share their experiences, feedback and suggestions on these schemes and initiatives, and to help determine local priorities. Discussions will also promote awareness of the new criminal laws, namely the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, digital transformation and strengthening of cooperatives, and initiatives for the protection and dignity of women and children, including Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat and Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan. As Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 culminates, the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 will also be discussed in the Gram Sabhas on 2nd October.
Citizens are earnestly invited to participate in their Special Gram Sabhas on 2nd October 2026 and contribute to the preparation of Panchayat Development Plans that reflect local needs and aspirations. Through “Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas”, Gram Sabhas will reinforce participatory governance and contribute to building Sashakt Panchayats, Atmanirbhar Panchayats and Viksit Panchayats in the larger endeavour of Viksit Bharat.

title: Sādhana Śhrinkhla: First Regional Workshop on Mission Karmayogi Concludes at Vijayawada
subtitle:
Workshop Anchors the Shift from Training to Capacity Building through UNNATI and Capacity Building Commission’s Training Institutions’ Transformation Framework

All Seven Participating States/Union Territories Present Best Practices and Action Plans to Transform Training Institutions into Capacity Building Institutions

Hon’ble Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh lauded CBC’s transformative initiatives to improve Civil Services Training Institution ecosystem across India
ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 OCT 2026 8:07PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The first Regional Workshop under
Sādhana Śhrinkhla
, organised by the Capacity Building Commission (CBC) on Mission Karmayogi, concluded on 30 September 2026 in Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh. The two-day workshop (29–30 September 2026) was themed "
From Training Institutions to Capacity Building Institutions
". It brought together more than 300 participants from Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Telangana, Odisha, Puducherry, Kerala and Tamil Nadu, along with Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) from these States/UTs. They included heads and faculty of Training Institutions, Administrative Training Institutes (ATIs), General Administration Departments and Academies.
Background
Sādhana
(Strengthening Adaptive Development and Humane Aptitude for National Advancement)
Śhrinkhla
is a nationwide series of regional consultative engagements. It builds on the stakeholder consultations organized by CBC previously, like -  National Training Conclave during Sādhana Saptah 2026 (2–8 April 2026), which focused on Technology, Tradition and Tangible Outcomes, and the National Departmental Summit on "Institutionalizing Capacity Building: From Training to Performance-linked Governance".
The regional workshops bring together concerned stakeholders to co-develop a Training Institute Transformation Framework reflecting their diverse needs and contexts. The workshops provide a platform to validate the framework and translate it into actionable priorities for a shared roadmap for transformation. Implementation will be anchored in UNNATI, the Framework’s core digital enabler, connecting over 900 Training Institutions to support resource sharing, collaboration and continuous, data-informed institutional improvement.
Day 1: Inaugural session
The workshop began with the lighting of the lamp and the
Karmayogi Gaan
. Dr. Alka Mittal, Member (Administration), CBC, delivered the welcome address. The gathering was addressed by Shri Peeyush Kumar, Principal Secretary (Planning), and Shri G. Sai Prasad, Chief Secretary, Government of Andhra Pradesh. A video on UNNATI was screened, and State felicitations were held.
Smt. S. Radha Chauhan, Chairperson, Capacity Building Commission, said that the capabilities of government officials must be continuously enhanced in view of rapidly changing technologies, particularly Artificial Intelligence. She said that "Nagrik Devo Bhava" has emerged as a core principle of governance, requiring officials to align their behaviour, skills and performance with the needs of citizens. She highlighted the role of iGOT Karmayogi in providing structured learning, and said that transforming TIs into strategic, competency-driven Capacity Building Institutions will help government organisations develop the capabilities their roles require and complement the online learning enabled at scale by iGOT Karmayogi.
Inaugurating the workshop, the Hon'ble Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, Shri Nara Chandrababu Naidu, said that technology and data have transformed governance. He said that real-time data, data integration across departments and AI-enabled monitoring can now support timely action, and that good policy must be matched by effective execution and leadership. He appreciated Mission Karmayogi, and its delivery channels - iGOT and UNNATI platforms for creating an integrated capacity-building ecosystem. He iterated that online learning must be complemented by physical training in institutions, and that continuous learning and unlearning is essential for every officer.
The Chief Minister congratulated the Andhra Pradesh government machinery for completing two crore courses on the iGOT Karmayogi portal. Referring to the State's
Swarna Andhra 2047
aspiration, he said that capable administration and effective policy execution are key to accelerating growth. He also highlighted the P4 (Public-Private-People Partnership) approach for spreading the benefits of development to the last mile. He welcomed UNNATI for connecting National, Regional and State Training Institutions on one platform, and suggested extending the network to universities and the private sector so that officials gain first-hand exposure to different working environments.
On the occasion, Andhra Pradesh was recognised as the top-performing State in capacity building of government employees, with Karnataka in second place and Odisha third. The awards were presented by the Chief Minister. The session concluded with a vote of thanks by Shri Jagdeep Gupta, Secretary, CBC.
Day 1: Technical sessions
Transformation from Training Institution to Capacity Building Institution: The first session, anchored through UNNATI, explained how TIs can move from delivering individual programmes to managing the complete capacity-building lifecycle. This covered understanding demand from Capacity Building Plans (CBPs), translating it into suitable learning interventions, and delivering them effectively. It included a demonstration of the AI CBP creation tool of iGOT Karmayogi, features of the UNNATI portal that translate the demands captured through CBPs for a Training Institution and how it enables a Training Institution to effectively deliver on them. All the participating State/UT’s also presented their progress on related Mission Karmayogi parameters.
Karmayogi Quality Framework (KQF) for TIs: The session explained how TIs can embed quality across the learning lifecycle, from identifying competency needs to designing, developing, delivering, evaluating and improving learning interventions. It introduced the Framework’s two complementary components: the National Curriculum Design Framework (NCDF) for competency-based curriculum design, and an AI-enabled Quality Evaluator for course review, supported by human review where needed.
Karmayogi Kartavya Karyakram (KKK): The session introduced the national behavioural training programme and its approach to building
Seva Bhav
among public servants, particularly at the grassroots. It explained how experiential learning, reflection and peer dialogue can strengthen citizen-centric attitudes and behaviour, and highlighted the role of TIs and faculty in taking the programme to the last mile.
Consultation on the Training Institution Transformation Framework: The session invited participants’ views on strengthening institutional governance, advancing digital transformation and making TIs AI-native. Participants discussed opportunities and challenges in operationalising CBC’s TI Transformation Framework, drawing on their respective State and institutional contexts. These deliberations informed the development of draft State Action Plans, identifying priorities and steps for implementation.
Day 2: Reflections, Expert Session and presentation of State Action Plans
Day 2 began with an expert session on "Rethinking Learning in the Age of AI", Shri Krishna Kumar, Founder and CEO, Simplilearn, highlighted that learning is no longer a stage of life but a continuous process. He noted that public servants now need AI fluency alongside domain expertise. He said that abundant content makes guidance scarce, so the trainer's role as mentor is more important than ever. He urged Training Institutions to adopt an AI-first curriculum, to emphasise learning by doing, and to use AI to scale learning.
Day 2 subsequently saw reflections on Day 1 by Shri Peeyush Kumar, Principal Secretary (Planning), Government of Andhra Pradesh. He summed up the main ideas from each session:
The shift from rule-based, course-centric training to role-based, competency-driven and outcome-oriented capacity building, with CBPs as the continuous source of demand.
Quality built into learning by design through the KQF.
Seva Bhav
developed through experience, reflection and peer dialogue under the KKK.
Three requirements for future-ready TIs that must advance together: a connected ecosystem, effective institutions and responsible AI adoption.
All seven participating States/UTs then presented their best practices and draft Action Plans, identifying priority areas for institutional strengthening and their requirements for adopting UNNATI. The Subject Matter Experts present also shared their key takeaways from the workshop.
Concluding address
In his concluding address, Shri Jagdeep Gupta, Secretary, Capacity Building Commission, summed up three themes from the deliberations. They correspond to the three pillars of the TI Transformation Framework:
Structural and Governance: empowered institutional leadership, calibrated autonomy and performance-linked accountability.
Operational Excellence and Ecosystem Collaboration: systematic sharing of faculty, knowledge and infrastructure across institutions through UNNATI.
Digital and AI Adoption: stronger digital infrastructure and secure use of AI tools, with final decisions remaining with people.
He requested States/UTs to finalise their Action Plans, incorporating the feedback received at the workshop. He also requested institutions not yet onboarded to join UNNATI.
About UNNATI
UNNATI (Unified New-Age National Training Initiative) is a digital platform launched by the CBC. It evolves the earlier NSCSTI accreditation into a continuous development ecosystem and connects over 700 Training Institutions across the country. It enables greater institutional visibility, collaboration and the systematic sharing of faculty, knowledge and infrastructure. It uses CBPs as a continuous demand signal for training, and it integrates with iGOT Karmayogi and State HR systems to track both online and offline learning. The UNNATI Capability Index provides real-time benchmarking of institutional performance. AI remains assistive, with final decisions resting with institutions and people.

Reaffirming the nation’s commitment to increasing the share of natural gas in the primary energy basket from current level of around 6%, the Minister also pointed to the momentum generated by National PNG Drive 2.0. During the West Asia crisis, the Government ensured continuity of essential gas supplies, while the CGD sector continued to expand PNG adoption and strengthen coordination with States and other stakeholders.
Addressing the gathering, the Secretary, Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, emphasized the evolving role of regulation in driving actual gas adoption across sectors, stressing that success must now be measured not merely by pipeline length laid, but by actual gas consumption, molecule utilization, and the speed at which household PNG connections multiply. He encouraged CGD entities to leverage special schemes to reduce cost recovery timelines from 10–15 years to 2–3 years, thereby addressing major financial roadblocks to network expansion. He also underlined the importance of coordination between upstream, downstream, Oil PSUs and the Government to ensure an uninterrupted clean energy supply.
The Minister also highlighted PNGRB’s technology-enabled approach to regulation through the National Hydrocarbon Infrastructure Monitoring System (NHIMS), which brings together infrastructure, administrative, transport, geographical and satellite data on a common digital platform. The system is expected to strengthen monitoring, planning and regulatory oversight and enable more informed and timely decision-making.
Looking ahead, the Minister underscored the need for faster and more effective digital grievance redressal, timely expansion of CGD networks into new areas, healthy competition, stronger sectoral capacity and a regulatory framework that keeps pace with India’s sustainability and Net Zero objectives. PNGRB’s continued independence and arm’s-length position from administrative and commercial interests, together with a clear, transparent and predictable regulatory framework, will remain important in building confidence across the industry.

title: Union Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas Shri Hardeep Singh Puri launches GOBARdhan Scheme to accelerate development of India’s Compressed Biogas sector
subtitle:
Integrated Central Sector Scheme brings assured offtake, stable pricing, capital assistance, pipeline connectivity, credit support and ecosystem development under a unified framework

GOBARdhan Handbook unveiled and Unified GOBARdhan Portal launched to support streamlined implementation of the Scheme
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 OCT 2026 8:27PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Shri Hardeep Singh Puri, today launched GOBARdhan, the Central Sector Scheme for development of the Compressed Biogas (CBG) sector.
The Scheme, approved by the Union Cabinet on 6 August 2026 with an outlay of ₹23,731 crore, provides a ten-year framework from FY 2026–27 to FY 2035–36 for accelerating CBG development in India. The scheme aims to increase domestic CBG production nearly 10-fold (to around 5 MMSCMD) with a long-term framework that gives investors and lenders greater certainty.
The launch brought together stakeholders from across the CBG ecosystem, including representatives of Central Ministries, State Governments, CBG developers, oil and gas companies, City Gas Distribution entities, financial institutions, cooperatives, technology providers and other stakeholders.
The launch featured the unveiling of the GOBARdhan Handbook, a comprehensive reference guide to assist stakeholders, project developers, State Governments and financial institutions in understanding the Scheme and navigating its CBG interventions, alongside the Unified GOBARdhan Portal, a centralised digital platform designed to streamline applications, eliminate multi-channel processes and enhance transparency throughout processing and implementation.
Speaking on the occasion, Shri Hardeep Singh Puri said that India’s growing energy requirements must be addressed through the combined objectives of availability, affordability and sustainability, with greater development of energy resources available within the country.
He said that CBG has particular relevance for India as it can convert crop residue, cattle dung and other organic resources into clean domestic energy, while generating organic manure and creating new economic opportunities in rural areas. Farmers, cooperatives, gaushalas and local enterprises can participate across feedstock collection, aggregation, transportation and processing, strengthening the circular link between agriculture and energy.
He called upon industry, financial institutions, States, cooperatives, technology providers and other stakeholders to translate the framework into operating plants and sustained CBG production, advancing India’s energy security, rural prosperity and the Prime Minister’s vision of Waste to Wealth and Annadata to Urjadata.
Addressing the gathering, Dr. Neeraj Mittal, Secretary, Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, highlighted that India currently meets nearly half of its natural gas requirement through imports and that CBG provides an opportunity to convert domestic organic waste into a domestic gas resource.
He said that the experience of the sector had also highlighted constraints relating to volatile revenues, fragmented support, limited long-term policy visibility, feedstock assurance, organic manure offtake and access to finance. GOBARdhan addresses these issues through the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas as the single nodal Ministry, predictable pricing, greater certainty of gas offtake, enhanced capital assistance, consolidated processes and greater use of digital monitoring.
The Secretary also highlighted the important role of State Governments in translating the national framework into projects on the ground, including through enabling State CBG policies, feedstock assessments, suitable land banks, faster approvals and infrastructure support.
An integrated framework for the CBG sector
A presentation on GOBARdhan outlined the Scheme architecture and the transition from multiple standalone interventions towards an integrated framework for the sector. GOBARdhan comprises six key interventions: CBG Offtake Assurance, CBG Pricing Framework, Capital Assistance for CBG Projects, Development of Pipeline Infrastructure, Credit Guarantee Support and the CBG Ecosystem Challenge Fund.
Under the offtake framework, CBG plants will be mapped to identified City Gas Distribution geographical areas or CBG clusters, enabling a dependable route to market. Under the CBG Obligation (CBO), the obligation to procure CBG rests with City Gas Distribution (CGD) entities. The procurement obligation has been prescribed at 3% in FY 2026–27, 4% in FY 2027–28 and 5% from FY 2028–29 onwards for the CNG (Transport) and PNG (Domestic) segment
The Scheme introduces an administered CBG price of ₹2,110 per MMBtu, providing greater revenue visibility to producers. Eligible greenfield projects can receive capital assistance of up to ₹2 crore per TPD of installed CBG capacity, including support for plant machinery, feedstock aggregation and FOM/LFOM processing and manure value-addition equipment.
To address gas evacuation constraints, support of up to 80% of eligible capital expenditure is available for pipelines connecting CBG clusters to trunk pipeline networks and up to 50% for standalone plants connecting to CGD networks.
A dedicated credit guarantee mechanism for eligible MSME-based CBG projects will cover up to 85% of the outstanding amount at default, subject to prescribed project limits. The guarantee cap is ₹20 crore per project for general MSME projects and ₹25 crore per project for women-led MSME projects, providing enhanced support to women entrepreneurs in the CBG sector.
The CBG Ecosystem Challenge Fund will support technology development, capacity building, feedstock assessment and aggregation, district-level ecosystem development and value addition in organic manure.
India’s CBG ecosystem has already established a foundation for further growth, with 217+ plants commissioned as of August 2026, with an installed capacity of more than 1,700 TPD. The Scheme aims to increase domestic CBG production nearly ten-fold over its ten-year implementation period.
The Scheme is expected to generate significant economic and environmental benefits, including more than ₹40,000 crore in foreign-exchange savings, over ₹75,000 crore added to GDP and more than 1.5 lakh jobs. It is also expected to replace 10 million tonnes of fossil fuel with clean gas, reduce more than 40 million tonnes of CO₂ emissions and support the production of 250 million tonnes of organic manure.

date:

content:
Promoting ‘Ease of living’ for the citizens and further simplifying toll-related procedures for Divyangjan & Persons with Disabilities (PwD), the Government of India has revised the guidelines for issuance and renewal of exempted FASTags for eligible Divyangjan/PwD beneficiaries. The revised framework is aimed at bringing greater uniformity in the issuance and renewal of exempted FASTag for eligible Divyangjan/PwD vehicles, while reducing the need for repeated procedural formalities. The guidelines will come into effect from 02nd October 2026.
Under this, exempted FASTags for vehicles specially designed and constructed for use by persons with physical disabilities, as well as vehicles registered under the ownership type ‘
Divyangjan
’, will be issued exempted FASTag based on the percentage of disability recorded in a valid Disability Certificate, Unique Disability Identity (UDID) Card or other applicable records.
Earlier guidelines mandated renewal of exempted FASTag for Divyangjan on annual basis.  However, as per the new guidelines, validity of the Exempted FASTag will be determined by the recorded percentage of disability. FASTag issued to persons with 70% to 100% disability will be valid for five years, while those issued to persons with 40% to less than 70% disability will be valid for three years. The exempted FASTag may be renewed thereafter, subject to continued eligibility and compliance with the provisions of the National Highways Fee Rules, 2008.
The revised provisions are aimed at making the National Highway tolling ecosystem more accessible, transparent and user-friendly for eligible Divyangjan/PwD beneficiaries, while ensuring that toll exemptions continue to be administered in accordance with the prescribed rules and eligibility requirements.

date:

content:
Key Highlights and Benefits:
First Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) tolling system implemented in Tamil Nadu at the Paranur Toll Plaza on the Tambaram – Tindivanam Section of NH-179B
Introduces barrier-less tolling, enabling vehicles to pass through toll locations without stopping
Significantly reduce human intervention in toll collection, saves fuel and time, cut down congestion, lower vehicular emissions, make toll operations more transparent and cost effective
Promotes barrier-free and seamless commuting, enhancing ‘Ease of Travel’ for the National Highway users
Leverages technologies such as Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) and FASTag to ensure seamless and efficient toll operations.
In a significant step towards transforming the Electronic Toll Collection system in the country, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has rolled out Tamil Nadu’s first Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) based tolling system at Paranur Toll Plaza on the Tambaram – Tindivanam Section of NH-179B. The MLFF system introduces barrier-less tolling, enabling vehicles to pass through toll locations without stopping. The system leverages advanced technologies such as Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) and FASTag-based Electronic Toll Collection to ensure seamless and efficient toll operations. The initiative aligns with the Government of India’s vision of delivering citizen centric services by leveraging technology for enhancing Ease of Living and Ease of Doing Business.
MLFF :
The introduction of MLFF marks a transformational shift in Electronic Toll Collection on National Highways. By eliminating the need for vehicles to stop at toll plazas, the system will significantly reduce human intervention in toll collection system, cut down congestion, improve travel time, enhance fuel efficiency and lower vehicular emissions on National Highways.
NHAI is implementing MLFF based tolling at various National Highways across the country in a phased manner. In order to provide a faster, seamless and barrier-free travel experience, NHAI has successfully rolled out the Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) tolling system at various locations in the country that includes Chorayasi Toll Plaza on Surat–Bharuch section of NH-48 in Gujarat; Mundka-Bakkarwala Toll Plaza on the Urban Extension Road-II (UER-II) in Delhi-NCR; Shahjahanpur, Daulatpura and Manoharpura Toll Plaza on Delhi–Jaipur section of NH-48 in Rajasthan; and Gharaunda Toll Plaza on the Panipat–Jalandhar section of National Highway-44 in Haryana.
For a seamless MLFF experience, National Highway users are required to maintain functional FASTag with sufficient balance to avoid Electronic Notice (E-Notice).
Implementation of MLFF has helped to strengthen the tolling ecosystem by enhancing transparency, reducing operational costs associated with setting up of physical toll plazas and improving overall efficiency in toll operations across the country.

title: Cooperation between the Nalanda University and the CSIR-Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (CSIR-TKDL) Unit for research and capacity-building in the areas of Traditional Knowledge (TK), Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), People’s Rights and Cultural Heritage
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 OCT 2026 9:26PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Nālandā University (NU) and the CSIR–Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (CSIR-TKDL) Unit have signed a Memorandum of Understanding today to establish a structured collaboration for academic, research and capacity-building cooperation in the areas of Traditional Knowledge (TK), Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), People’s Rights and Cultural Heritage, including Traditional Cultural Expressions (TCEs). The MoU was signed by Prof. Sachin Chaturvedi, Vice Chancellor, Nālandā University and Dr. Viswajanani J Sattigeri, Scientist-H and Head, CSIR-TKDL Unit, in the presence of the faculty members of the Nālandā University and senior officials of the CSIR-TKDL Unit.
Through the collaboration, the two organizations, Nālandā University and CSIR-TKDL Unit shall draw together their individual strengths to address their common interests on matters of TK, IPR, cultural heritage including the TCEs of Bihar. The cooperation shall focus on academic and research activities and intellectual exchanges, trainings, student internship and exchange visits and networking, among others.
Speaking on the occasion, Prof. Chaturvedi, Vice-Chancellor, Nālandā University, appreciated the significant efforts of the CSIR on the TKDL and its role in preventing the misappropriation India’s TK. He further noted that this collaboration would strengthen efforts to identify, document and disseminate TK and TCEs while creating greater awareness about IPRs and also training the younger generation on the matter. He highlighted the importance of systematically documenting, preserving, and making TK across subject areas such as ecological knoweldge of the communities, folklore, music, and others. He also opined that the TK may be made accessible in a manner that safeguards the interests of knowledge holders and communities, as well as the organizations’ commitment to evidence based R&D in Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS). He observed that the collaboration with TKDL would provide an important platform for integrating TK with contemporary academic research, documentation, IP awareness and interdisciplinary scholarship.
Dr. Sattigeri, Head, CSIR-TKDL Unit stated that India has been leading globally on all matters of TK, be it policies or initiatives such as the TKDL. She stated that the ancient Nālandā University speaks of the importance of collaboration between organizations, both nationally and internationally. This collaboration between CSIR-TKDL Unit with the new Nālandā University is envisaged to rejuvenate the past glory of Nalanda as both educational and research hub, with specific focus on the cultural heritage of India, and particularly, Bihar.
The Parties are confident that the collaboration between Nālandā University and CSIR-TKDL Unit will contribute to the attainment of the objectives of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and National IPR Policy 2016 on TK, IPR and cultural heritage.
About Nālandā University:
Nālandā University has been established as an International University of “National Importance” under the aegis of the Ministry of External Affairs, Govt of India, at Rajgir, District-Nalanda, Bihar. The objectives of Nālandā University, deriving on its ancient heritage value and strong international cooperation,  are focused on the pursuit of intellectual, philosophical, historical and spiritual studies and others. The revival of Nālandā University aims at improving regional understanding and the appreciation of one another’s heritage and history, to build a community of learning where students, scholars, researchers and academicians can work together symbolizing the spirituality that unites all mankind.
About TKDL:
The TKDL database, first of its kind worldwide, was established in 2001 by the Government of India, through a collaboration between CSIR and Ministry of AYUSH. The key objective of the TKDL is to prevent the erroneous grant of patents on Indian traditional knowledge (TK) and deter misappropriation of the country’s heritage. Currently, the TKDL contains information on over 5.2 lakh formulations and practices of Indian Systems of Medicine such as Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha, and Sowa Rigpa as well as Yoga from the traditional texts. The TK information from diverse languages and subject areas are transcribed into value-added information correlated with modern terminologies.
The TKDL information is presented in a digitized format in five international languages including English, German, French, Japanese and Spanish, therein breaking language and format barriers for ease of use by patent examiners. Currently, the TKDL database is available to 18 international patent offices through Non-Disclosure Agreements.
The TKDL is a global benchmark in the defensive protection of traditional knowledge and has been successful in protecting India’s interest against any possible misuse of its heritage. The impact has been significant, with over 375 patent applications world-over being revoked, rejected, amended, withdrawn or abandoned, based on the prior art evidences presented from the TKDL database.

title: Government Strengthens Implementation of PCR and SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Acts through Special Courts, Victim Support, Awareness and Grievance Redressal Mechanisms
subtitle: Central assistance of ₹1,423.30 crore released to States and Union Territories over three financial years for implementation of the PCR and PoA Acts
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 OCT 2026 1:29PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Central Government continues to support States and Union Territories in the effective implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, through a range of measures aimed at strengthening enforcement mechanisms, facilitating speedy trial, providing relief and rehabilitation to victims, creating awareness about statutory safeguards and promoting social harmony.
The implementation of the two Acts primarily rests with the State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. The Government of India, through the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for implementation of the PCR Act, 1955 and the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, provides financial assistance to States and UTs for strengthening the institutional and implementation mechanisms under the Acts and Rules.
Strengthening Exclusive Special Courts for Speedy Trial
As reported by States and Union Territories, 217 Exclusive Special Courts have been established in 15 States and Union Territories for trial of offences under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989. The Act also provides for designation of Courts of Session as Special Courts in districts where the number of cases is relatively lower, with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court.
The establishment and strengthening of Exclusive Special Courts is aimed at facilitating speedy trial and effective disposal of cases under the Act and ensuring that victims have access to specialised judicial mechanisms.
Central Assistance to States and UTs
Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme, the Centre released ₹392.71 crore in 2022–23, ₹535.30 crore in 2023–24 and ₹495.29 crore in 2024–25, amounting to ₹1,423.30 crore over the three financial years, to States and Union Territories.
The scheme provides assistance for strengthening of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Protection Cells and Special Police Stations, strengthening of judicial machinery, relief and rehabilitation of victims, incentives for inter-caste marriages, awareness generation and other measures for effective implementation of the Acts.
Over the same three years, 88,172, 79,667 and 99,216 victims, respectively, were reported to have received relief under the scheme.
Promoting Awareness of Legal Safeguards
The Government has accorded priority to creating wider awareness about the legal safeguards and rights available to members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and the Rules framed thereunder.
Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme, States and UTs are supported in undertaking awareness campaigns, workshops, training programmes, awareness camps and other outreach activities to disseminate information about the provisions of the Acts and Rules.
SAMBAL – Strengthening Access to Grievance Redressal
To facilitate easier access to grievance redressal mechanisms, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment launched the National Helpline Against Atrocities (NHAA) in December 2021, subsequently renamed SAMBAL. The initiative provides members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes with an accessible mechanism to register and track grievances relating to the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. The helpline is available through toll-free number 1800-202-1989 and short code 14566.
Encouraging Social Integration through Inter-Caste Marriages
As part of the Government’s efforts to promote social integration, equality and social harmony, financial assistance is provided under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for inter-caste marriages where one of the spouses belongs to a Scheduled Caste.
The number of couples reported to have received incentive for inter-caste marriages increased from 14,225 in 2022-23 to 26,050 in 2024–25.
According to the latest
Crime in India
figures provided in the source document, 65,646 cases were registered under the Act in 2024, compared with 70,725 in 2023 and 67,633 in 2022. At the end of 2024, 3,92,006 cases were pending trial. These figures underline the continuing need for timely investigation, effective prosecution and prompt support to victims.
The Government remains committed to working with States and Union Territories to strengthen implementation of the Act and ensure access to justice for members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

title: Forward-Looking Survey on Private Corporate Sector CAPEX Investment Intentions

date:
